In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

﴿A surah which We have sent down and made obligatory.﴾

Tafsir of Surat al-Nur

It is a Madinan surah. Al-Hakim Abu 'Abd Allah al-Hafiz related, in what he transmitted as an addition to the Two Sahihs, through the narration of Shu'ayb ibn Ishaq, from al-Zuhri, from 'Urwah, from 'A'ishah (may Allah be pleased with her), that the Prophet (ﷺ) said concerning women: "Do not settle them in upper chambers, do not teach them writing, and teach them spinning and Surat al-Nur."

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿A surah which We have sent down﴾. The reading of al-'A'raj and Mujahid is "Surah anzalnaha" (with the word surah in the accusative). A surah (sura) is a collection of verses from what Allah the Exalted has sent down, with a known beginning and end. The word surah is put in the nominative because its meaning is: "This is a surah." Its being in the accusative ("surah") would have the sense: "We sent down a surah."

His saying: ﴿and made obligatory﴾ is read with the shaddah (tashdid) and without it (takhfif). As for the reading without shaddah (faradnaha), it has two meanings: first, "We obligated you to act upon what is made obligatory in it"; second, "We set forth (faradnaha) what is in it of the prescribed limits (hudud)." Al-fard means taqdir (determination), and from it is His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿so half of what you have determined (faradtum)﴾, meaning what you have determined. As for the reading with shaddah (farradnaha), it has two meanings:

The first: "We made its obligations (fara'id) obligatory," and it was emphasized (shaddada) because of the multitude of what it contains.

The second meaning: "We made it clear (faradnaha) and detailed it."

Mujahid said: It is the command to what is lawful and the prohibition of what is unlawful.

His saying: ﴿And We sent down therein clear verses﴾, meaning: manifest proofs.

His saying: ﴿that you may remember﴾, meaning: that you may take heed.

The words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿The adulterous woman and the adulterer﴾. The people of knowledge said: He began with the woman because tenderness of heart toward them is greater, so He began with them lest the establishing of the hadd (prescribed punishment) be neglected for them, and their matter be left to the men. Others among them said: because desire is stronger in women, and adultery is the result of desire. And in the hadd for theft He began with the man, because strength and boldness are greater in men, and theft is the result of strength and boldness. This is a good opinion.

As for His words: ﴿Flog each one of them with a hundred lashes﴾. Al-jald (flogging) is striking the skin. It is said: "jaldtuhu" when I struck his skin, "batantuhu" when I struck his belly, and "zahartuhu" when I struck his back. Regarding this verse there are two opinions. The first: the verse is general concerning virgins and previously married persons, so the previously married person is flogged along with being stoned. It is narrated from Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, that "he flogged Shurahah al-Hamdaniyyah on Thursday one hundred lashes, and stoned her on Friday, and said: 'I flogged her by the Book of Allah, and I stoned her by the Sunnah of the Messenger of Allah.'"

As for the view of the majority of scholars, it is that the verse is specific to virgins, and that the previously married person is stoned and not flogged. The people of knowledge agreed that this verse was abrogated, because the ruling mentioned concerning confinement (imsak) is in Surat an-Nisa'.

It has been narrated from Ubadah ibn al-Samit, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Prophet (ﷺ) received revelation while we were with him, and when revelation came down upon him his face would change, and we would turn our eyes away from him. When it passed from him he said: "Take from me, take from me. Allah has made a way for them (women): the previously married man with the previously married woman is stoned, and the virgin with the virgin is flogged one hundred lashes and exiled for a year."

Al-Naqqash mentioned that in the reading of Ubayy ibn Ka'b in Surat al-Ahzab: "The old man and the old woman, if they commit adultery, then stone them absolutely as a punishment from Allah, and Allah is Mighty, Wise."

Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, intended to write this on the margin of the Mushaf, but then left it lest what is not of the Qur'an be attached to the Qur'an.

As for His words: ﴿And let not kindness for them overcome you in the religion of Allah﴾. It was read as "rafah" without a hamzah, and in an irregular reading as "ra'fah," meaning mercy. Know that mercy and tenderness are a feeling in the heart that is not forbidden, because it arises in the heart without a person's choice. The meaning of the verse is only: the application of mercy in (suspending the hadd) and lightening it.

It is narrated from Abdullah ibn Umar that he struck a slave-girl of his with the hadd, as she had committed adultery, and he began striking her leg and back. His son Salim said to him: ﴿And let not kindness for them overcome you in the religion of Allah﴾. He said: "O my son, Allah did not command me to kill her, nor to strike her head, and she has been struck and has been hurt." The people of knowledge have said: one should exert oneself in flogging the adulterer more than one exerts oneself in flogging the drinker of wine, because of the explicit text of the Book.

(And His words: ﴿in the religion of Allah﴾ means: in the judgment of Allah.)

As for His words: ﴿If you believe in Allah and the Last Day﴾, its meaning is apparent.

The true meaning of it: the believer is not seized by mercy or tenderness when the command of the Lord comes.

As for His words: ﴿And let a group of the believers witness their punishment﴾, Ibn Abbas said: one or more. It is narrated from Ata: from one man up to a thousand men. It is narrated from Sa'id ibn Jubayr and Ikrimah: two men. It is narrated from al-Zuhri and Qatadah: three persons. Malik said: four persons, and this is the view of al-Shafi'i and a group of the people of knowledge.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 24, verse 3:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿The fornicator does not marry except a fornicatress or an idolatress﴾. There are several opinions regarding this verse. The first: that ﴿The fornicator does not marry except a fornicatress or an idolatress, and the fornicatress is not married except by a fornicator or an idolater, and that is forbidden to the believers﴾ was revealed concerning a woman called Umm Mahzul, who was a prostitute (baghiyy); when she married a man, she stipulated that he would spend on her. A man from among the Companions of the Messenger of Allah wished to marry her, so he asked the Prophet (ﷺ), and Allah the Exalted revealed this verse: ﴿The fornicator does not marry except a fornicatress﴾. It is also said that the woman's name was ʿAnaq. This is the statement of ʿAbdullah ibn ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAs.

The second opinion: Mujahid, Qatadah and others said: "There were prostitutes in Medina who had banners on their doors by which they were recognised, and they were accommodating to men. When the Companions of the Messenger of Allah migrated to Medina, some of the poor among the Emigrants wished to marry them so that they would spend on them, so Allah the Exalted revealed this verse."

The third opinion: It is narrated from al-Hasan al-Basri that he said: the meaning of the verse is: "The fornicator who has been flogged does not marry except a fornicatress who has been flogged, and the fornicatress who has been flogged is not married except by a fornicator who has been flogged." In some of the Musnads, this opinion is narrated from the Prophet through the route of Abu Hurayrah.

The fourth opinion: It is narrated from ʿAli ibn Abi Talhah al-Walibi, from Ibn ʿAbbas, that the meaning of the verse is: the fornicator does not commit fornication except with a fornicatress, and the meaning of nikah [here] is wat' (sexual intercourse). Al-Zajjaj said: this opinion is weak, because the word nikah in the sense of wat' has not occurred in the Qur'an.

The fifth opinion - and it is the best of the opinions - is the statement of Saʿid ibn al-Musayyab: that the verse is abrogated (mansukhah), and in the ruling of Islam it was not permissible for a fornicator to marry the one he had fornicated with. ʿAbdullah ibn Masʿud said: If a fornicator marries a fornicatress, they are both fornicators forever. Saʿid ibn al-Musayyab said: Then this was abrogated by His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And marry off the single (ayama) among you﴾, and the fornicatress is an ayyim, so it is permissible for her to be married by a fornicator and others. The evidence that the ruling now is this is what is narrated from Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may Allah be pleased with him, that he was sitting in the mosque and ʿUmar was with him, when a man came, distraught, and he had a stain (lawth). Abu Bakr said: This man has come about a matter; ask him, O ʿUmar. So ʿUmar said to him: What is your affair? He mentioned that a guest had come to him, and the guest had fornicated with his daughter. ʿUmar said to him: May Allah disgrace you, and he struck his chest and said: Why did you not conceal your daughter? Then he summoned the man and the woman, and Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, ordered that they be flogged the prescribed flogging, (then he married the woman to the man). Abu ʿUbayd, may Allah have mercy on him, mentioned that it is disliked for a man to marry a woman of immorality, and if his wife commits fornication, it is recommended for him to divorce her. He said: As for the report narrated from the Prophet that a man came to him and said: "My wife does not turn away the hand of a touching man (lamis)," so he said: "Divorce her." He said: "I love her." He said: "Enjoy her." Abu [ʿUbayd] said: this report is transmitted through two narrations, each of which is mursal, so this is not established from the Prophet. And even if it were established, it is possible that his saying "my wife does not turn away the hand of a touching man" means that she spends whatever comes into her hand and gives it away, and it seems he complained of her extravagance and the squandering of his wealth; the intended meaning is not that she commits fornication, for it is not permissible to mention that before the Prophet and then he orders him to keep her.

As for His saying: ﴿And that is forbidden to the believers﴾, its meaning is clear, and we have explained that this is abrogated.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 24, verse 4:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And those who accuse chaste women﴾. Al-muhsanat (the chaste women) are those who have guarded themselves (ahsanna anfusahunna).

And His saying: ﴿then do not produce four witnesses﴾, meaning: to their fornication. The "casting" (ramy) mentioned in the verse is the qadhf (slanderous accusation) of fornication.

And His saying: ﴿lash them eighty lashes﴾, meaning: strike them with eighty whips.

And His saying: ﴿and never accept their testimony ever after﴾. The early scholars (al-salaf) differed on this. It is narrated from Shurayh, al-Hasan, Ibrahim al-Nakha'i and a group that they said: the testimony of the slanderer is never accepted ever, once he has received the prescribed punishment, even if he repents. This is the view of the people of Iraq (ahl al-'Iraq).

Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz, al-Zuhri, Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, al-Sha'bi and a group said: if he repents, his testimony is accepted. This is the view of the people of the Hijaz (ahl al-Hijaz).

Al-Sha'bi said: "God accepts his repentance, and you do not accept his testimony?!" Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib related that Umar said to Abu Bakra: "Repent, and your testimony will be accepted." He did not repent. The matter is well known.

And His saying: ﴿And those are the defiantly disobedient, except those who repent﴾. As for the one who said that the testimony of the slanderer is accepted after repentance, he went to the view that

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 24, verse 5:

His saying: ﴿Except those who repent﴾ refers to everything apart from the hadd (the prescribed punishment). It is related from al-Sha'bi that the hadd also falls away through repentance. As for those who held that the testimony of the slanderer is not accepted after repentance, they said: His saying ﴿Except those who repent﴾ refers to His saying ﴿And those are the defiantly disobedient (al-fasiqun)﴾. If it is said: If you accept the testimony of the slanderer after repentance, then what is the meaning of His saying, exalted is He, ﴿ever﴾? The answer to this: al-Zajjaj said in his book: The "abad" (lifetime, duration) of every person is his term according to what befits his case. So when it is said, "The testimony of the disbeliever is not accepted ever," what is meant is for as long as he remains a disbeliever; and when it is said, "The testimony of the slanderer is not accepted ever," what is meant is for as long as he remains a slanderer. As for the repentance of the slanderer, it is by retracting his own statement, and it is said: by his regret over what he committed.

His saying: ﴿And amend﴾ means: they remain steadfast in repentance.

His saying: ﴿Then indeed Allah is Forgiving, Merciful﴾ has already been explained earlier.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 24, verse 6:

His saying: ﴿And those who accuse their spouses⦆ means: they accuse their wives of adultery.

And His saying: ﴿and have no witnesses except themselves⦆ means: other than themselves.

And His saying: ﴿then the testimony of one of them is four⦆, with the nominative (marfu') reading, and it has also been recited with the accusative (nasb) "four". As for the nominative, its implied sense is: then the testimony of one of them, which averts the hadd punishment, is four, so it is nominative as the predicate of the subject (khabar al-ibtida'). As for the accusative, its implied sense is: then the testimony of one of them is that he bears witness four times.

And His saying: ﴿four testimonies by Allah that he is certainly among the truthful⦆ means: regarding what he has accused her of, namely adultery.

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And the fifth [testimony] is that the curse of Allah be upon him﴾. It has also been recited as "أَن لعنة الله عَلَيْهِ" (anna la'nata Allahi 'alayhi) with the nun of "anna" pronounced with sukun (silent). Its meaning is: "that it is the curse of Allah upon him." Sibawayh recited a line of poetry:

(In a company of youths like Indian swords, they have known / that surely every one who hides and goes barefoot is destroyed.)

He means: that he is destroyed.

And His words: ﴿if he is among the liars﴾ mean: in what he accused her of, namely adultery.

Allah's saying: ﴿And it averts from her the punishment﴾. Regarding "the punishment" there are two opinions: one of them is that it is the hadd (the prescribed legal punishment), and the other is that it is imprisonment (al-habs). The interpretation as hadd is more apparent, because Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿And let a group of the believers witness their punishment﴾, meaning the hadd.

And His saying: ﴿That she bear witness four times by Allah that he is surely among the liars﴾ means: concerning what he accused her of, namely adultery (al-zina).

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 24, verse 9:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And the fifth [testimony is] that the curse of Allah be upon her if he is among the truthful.﴾ It was also read: "أَن غضب الله عَلَيْهَا" (anna ghadaba Allahu ʿalayha), and it was read: "أَن غضب الله عَلَيْهَا" with the ḍād vowelled with a kasra (anna ghaḍiba Allahu ʿalayha). So His saying ﴿أَن غضب الله عَلَيْهَا﴾ (an ghaḍiba) is a verb, and His saying ﴿أَن غضب الله عَلَيْهَا﴾ (anna) is a noun [in the sense of the particle with its noun], and His saying {أَن غضب الله} is also a verb, meaning: that the anger of Allah [be upon her].

His saying ﴿if he is among the truthful﴾ means: in what he accused her of, namely adultery. The occasion of revelation of the verse is what Ibn ʿAbbas narrated: that Hilal ibn Umayya accused his wife of [adultery] with Shurayk ibn Samhaʾ before the Prophet. The Prophet said to him: "Produce evidence, or else the punishment will be inflicted on your back." Hilal said: "O Messenger of Allah, by Him who sent you with the truth, I am indeed truthful, and Allah will send down what will clear my back from the punishment." So this verse was revealed. The Messenger of Allah summoned Hilal and his wife and had them perform mutual oath-cursing (li'an) between them. Hilal began and swore four times, and when he reached the fifth, the Prophet said to him: "Stop, for it is decisive." Hilal said: "Allah knows that I am truthful," and he bore witness with the fifth [oath]. Then the woman stood up and swore four times, and when she reached the fifth, the Prophet said to her: "Stop, for it is decisive." Ibn ʿAbbas said: "She hesitated for a while, until we thought she would retract. Then she said: 'I will not disgrace my people today,' and she bore witness with the fifth [oath]." The Prophet said: "If she gives birth to a child with dark eyes, large buttocks and thick calves, then it belongs to Shurayk ibn Samhaʾ." She gave birth to him with this description. The Prophet said: "Had it not been for the oaths, there would have been a matter between me and her." The report is authentic.

And from ʿAbd Allah ibn Masʿud, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said: "We were sitting in the mosque on a Friday night, and with us was a man who went out from us and entered his house, and he found a man with his wife. He came to the Prophet and complained to him. He said: 'Bring witnesses.' He said: 'And how can I have witnesses?' He said: 'Indeed, you have been overwhelmed in this matter, for if the man is killed, you would kill him; if he speaks, you would punish him; and if he remains silent, he remains silent in rage. O Allah, decide.' Then Allah revealed these verses." In a third narration: when Allah, may He be exalted, revealed ﴿And those who accuse chaste women and do not bring four witnesses... [to the end of the verse]﴾, Saʿd ibn ʿUbada said: "O Messenger of Allah, what do you think? If I found a man lying with a woman [who is] a lady, should I not disturb him or move him until I bring four witnesses? By the time I bring the witnesses, the man will have finished his need." The Prophet said: "Look, O assembly of the Ansar, at what your chief says." They said: "O Messenger of Allah, he is a jealous man, and he has never married a woman except a virgin, and he has never divorced a woman, so any of us would love to marry her." Saʿd said: "I know that what Allah has revealed is true, but I was surprised." So Allah revealed the verse of li'an, as we have explained.

There are many reports on this subject, including the hadith of ʿAsim ibn ʿAdi, [and ʿUwaymir] al-ʿAjlani and others, and this is mentioned in the books of hadith.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 24, verse 10:

His statement, may He be exalted: ﴿And were it not for the grace of Allah upon you and His mercy, and that Allah is Accepting of repentance, Merciful﴾.

The response (jawab) to this verse is omitted, and similar to it is the saying of a man when someone reviles him: "O man, were it not for such-and-such," meaning: "Were it not for such-and-such, I would have reviled you." Accordingly, the meaning of His statement, ﴿And were it not for the grace of Allah upon you and His mercy﴾, is: the liar among you two would have immediately received the punishment. Others have said: ﴿And were it not for the grace of Allah upon you and His mercy﴾ refers to the delay of the punishment and His granting respite, for He would have hastened His punishment.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 24, verse 11:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Indeed, those who came with the slander are a faction among you﴾. These verses concern the story of ʿĀʾishah (may Allah be pleased with her). The occasion of their revelation is what al-Zuhri narrated from ʿUrwah, Saʿid ibn al-Musayyib, ʿAlqamah ibn Waqqas and ʿUbayd Allah ibn ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿUtbah, all of them from ʿĀʾishah (may Allah be pleased with her), that she said: "When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) went out on a journey, he would draw lots among his wives. He went out on a campaign he undertook, and he drew lots among his wives, and my lot came out." In one narration, the campaign was the campaign of Muraysi'. In another narration, the campaign was the campaign of Banu al-Mustaliq. She said: "When we returned near Medina, the Messenger of Allah halted for a night. Then they announced the departure, so I went out for my need. When I had finished my business, I returned and searched for my necklace, and I found that a necklace of mine made of Zifar onyx had fallen off. So I went back, and the men who used to load my howdah came and placed the howdah on the camel, and they thought I was inside it. Women in those days were light, for they ate only a little food. So I returned after the army had moved on, and there was neither a caller nor an answerer. Safwan ibn al-Mu'attal al-Sulami had lagged behind the army." In one narration, he used to make a habit of lagging behind, so that if anyone dropped something or left something behind, he would take it and return it to its owner. He came after me, and he said the words "Inna lillah" and did not speak a word to me, and my veil had fallen. He made his camel kneel and stepped on its foreleg for me until I mounted it, and he came leading me until we caught up with the army, and they had halted at the height of the midday heat. She said: "When we reached the army, people spoke, and those who were destroyed were destroyed," the report in its full length.

The Shaykh and Imam said: This hadith was related to us by al-Makki ibn ʿAbd al-Razzaq al-Kushmihani, who said: my grandfather Abu al-Haytham ibn Muhammad ibn Yusuf al-Firabri related to us [that he said]: Muhammad ibn Isma'il al-Bukhari related to us: Abu al-Rabi' al-Zahrani related to us from Fulayh ibn Sulayman, from al-Zuhri… the report.

It is narrated that the revelation was delayed for [thirty-]seven days.

In this report, ʿĀʾishah fell ill and asked the Messenger of Allah for permission, and she returned to her father's house. The Messenger of Allah used to enter [her quarters] before she returned to her father's house while she was ill, and he would say: "How are you?" Then, when she returned to her father's house, she learned the news from the mother of Mistah, so her illness increased and she wept, and her tears would not stop, until weeping nearly split her heart. She mentioned this to her mother, and her mother said to her: "Be at ease. Rarely is a beautiful woman with a man who has co-wives without people speaking about her."

In this report, the Prophet called ʿAli and Usamah ibn Zayd and consulted them. As for ʿAli, he said: "O Messenger of Allah, there are many women." As for Usamah, he said: "I know nothing of her but good. Ask the slave girl," meaning Barirah. So he asked Barirah, and she said: "I know nothing of her except that she is a young girl who kneads dough, and a domestic sheep comes and eats her dough."

In this report, the Prophet came to the house of Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him) after the period we mentioned had passed, and said: "O ʿĀʾishah, if you have committed a sin, repent to Allah, for Allah accepts repentance." She said: "My tears dried up until I could not find a drop of them. Then I said: If I say that I did it, and Allah knows that I did not do it, they will not believe me; and if I say: I did not do it, and Allah knows that I did not do it, they will not believe me either. I do not find an example for me and for you except the saying of the father of Yusuf, whose name I have forgotten: ﴿So patience is most fitting, and Allah is the one sought for help against what you describe﴾." Then I withdrew, and the Messenger of Allah [] received the revelation. She said: "I considered myself too insignificant to think that Allah would reveal about me a Qur'an to be recited, but I thought he might see a dream. But when the revelation overcame him, I was not frightened, because I knew that I was innocent, and Allah knows that."

In some narrations: my parents nearly had their souls leave them out of fear. When the state passed from the Messenger of Allah, he said: "Rejoice, O ʿĀʾishah, for Allah the Exalted has revealed your innocence," and he recited the verses: ﴿Indeed, those who came with the slander are a faction among you﴾. My father said to me: "Stand up and go to the Messenger of Allah." My mother said: "Stand up and go to the Messenger of Allah." I said: "I will not stand, and I will praise none but Allah, for Allah the Exalted has revealed my innocence."

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Indeed, those who came with the slander are a faction among you﴾. Al-Ifk is the most extreme lie, and it is so named because it is turned away (maṣrūf) from the truth. His saying: ﴿a faction among you﴾. These are the faction: ʿAbd Allah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul, Mistah ibn Uthathah, the son of Abu Bakr's maternal aunt, Hassan ibn Thabit, Hamnah bint Jahsh, wife of Talhah ibn ʿAbd Allah, sister of Zaynab, and a number of others. The ʿusbah (faction) is ten or more.

His saying: ﴿Do not think it bad for you; rather, it is good for you﴾. This is an address to ʿĀʾishah and Safwan ibn al-Mu'attal, for they both were slandered together. Some said: it is an address to ʿĀʾishah, her parents, the Prophet and Safwan. The meaning of the verse: do not think it bad for you, that is, this slander is good for you because of the reward, and what Allah has stored up for them of that.

His saying: ﴿For every man among them is what he earned of sin﴾, meaning: of sin in proportion to what he earned.

His saying: ﴿And the one who took upon himself its greater part﴾. It was read as "kibrahu" and al-A'raj read "kubrahu". His saying "kibrahu" means his sin. His saying "kubrahu" means its greater part, the majority of it. The poet said: (She sleeps, unaware of the greatness of her affair, but when she rises slowly, she nearly stumbles.)

As for the one who took upon himself its greater part, most say he is ʿAbd Allah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul. As for the great punishment, it is the Fire in the Hereafter.

Masruq related that Hassan ibn Thabit asked permission to enter upon ʿĀʾishah, and she permitted him. Masruq said: "Do you permit him, when he said what he said?" She said: "He has been struck by the great punishment," and he had become blind. Hassan repented of that statement and praised ʿĀʾishah, saying:

(A chaste, noble woman who is never suspected of doubt, and who wakes up hungry from the flesh of the heedless.)

(If what has reached me that I said it is true, then may my whip never be raised to my fingers.)

It is reported from Abu ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAla' that he denied "kibr" and said: "Kibr refers only to patronage (walāʾ) and lineage (nasab)." Others mentioned that each of the two readings is sound, and we have explained this.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 24, verse 12:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Why, when you heard it, did the believing men and believing women not think well of their own kind?﴾ That is, of those who are like themselves. This is like the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "The believers are like one soul," and Allah, may He be exalted, said: ﴿And do not kill yourselves﴾, meaning that some of you should not kill others. It is also said that the meaning of "thought" (ẓann) here is "was certain" (ayqana).

And His saying: ﴿And they said, "This is a clear falsehood."﴾ That is, an evident lie.

"His saying: ﴿Why did they not bring four witnesses for it?﴾ That is: concerning what they claimed.

And His saying: ﴿So when they do not bring the witnesses, then those, with Allah, they are the liars.﴾ If someone says: how can they become liars with Allah when they did not bring the witnesses, (and whoever is a liar is a liar with Allah whether he brings the witnesses or does not bring them)? The answer: we say: some of them said: ﴿with Allah﴾ means: in the judgment of Allah. And some of them said: ﴿with Allah, they are the liars﴾ means: they are the liars in what Allah has commanded you [to believe]. The third answer: this is in reference to ʿĀʾishah, may Allah be pleased with her, so its meaning is: those are the liars concerning my unseen and my knowledge."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Qur'an) on surah 24, verse 14:

The Most High's saying: ﴿And were it not for Allah's bounty upon you and His mercy in this world and the Hereafter, a great punishment would have touched you for what you plunged into.﴾ "Afadtum" means: you plunged (khadtum) into it. And His saying: ﴿a great punishment﴾ means: a punishment without end. Thus said Ibn 'Abbas, and he interpreted it this way because the Most High has mentioned that the one who took upon himself its greater part was touched by a great punishment. Likewise, the great punishment is in this world, and it has already touched him, for he was flogged with the hadd penalty (hadd, the prescribed punishment). As for the punishment that has no end, it has not touched him in this world; rather, it will touch him in the Hereafter.

And 'Amrah narrated from 'A'ishah: "When these verses were revealed, the Prophet (ﷺ) applied the hadd penalty to four persons: 'Abd Allah ibn Ubayy, Hassan ibn Thabit, Mistah ibn Uthathah, and Hamnah bint Jahsh."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 24, verse 15:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿When you received it with your tongues﴾, meaning: some of you convey it to others, and some of you narrate it from one another. It is related from ʿĀʾishah that she recited: "When you received it with your tongues, the lie" (idh talaqqūnahu bi-alsinatikum al-kadhib). It is also said: it means hastening in lying.

And His saying: ﴿and you say with your mouths what you have no knowledge of, and you reckon it to be trivial﴾, meaning: light (khafīf).

﴿And it is, with Allah, tremendous﴾, meaning: great (kabīr).

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 24, verse 16:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Why, when you heard it, did you not say﴾. Its meaning: "Why did you not, when you heard it..."

﴿"It is not for us to speak of this. Glory be to You! This is a tremendous slander."﴾ Al-buhtan (slander) is lying in a manner that leaves one dumbfounded (al-kadhib ʿala al-mukabara). It is said: "bahatahu" when you tell him of his lie to his face. In some reports: Umm Ayyub al-Ansari said to Abu Ayyub: "Has it not reached you what is said about ʿA'isha?" Abu Ayyub said: "It is not for us to speak of this. Glory be to You! This is a tremendous slander." He said this before the verse was revealed, and then the verse was revealed in accordance with his words.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 24, verse 17–18:

His saying: ﴿God admonishes you never to return to the like of it﴾. Mujahid said: God forbids you to return to the like of it, ever.

﴿If you are believers. And God makes the signs clear to you﴾: that is, the proofs (al-dalalat).

﴿And God is All-Knowing, All-Wise﴾: All-Knowing of His creation, All-Wise in His action.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 24, verse 17–18:

His saying: ﴿God admonishes you never to return to the like of it﴾. Mujahid said: God forbids you to return to the like of it, ever.

﴿If you are believers. And God makes the signs clear to you﴾: that is, the proofs (al-dalalat).

﴿And God is All-Knowing, All-Wise﴾: All-Knowing of His creation, All-Wise in His action.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 24, verse 19:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Indeed, those who love that indecency should spread among those who have believed﴾, means: that it should be spread abroad and become well known.

﴿Among those who have believed﴾, i.e., ʿĀʾishah, Ṣafwān, and the family of Abū Bakr. Their spreading of it was that some of them would meet others and say to him: "Has it not reached you such-and-such about ʿĀʾishah?"

And His saying: ﴿For them is a painful punishment in this world and the Hereafter﴾. The punishment in this world is the prescribed penalty (ḥadd), and the punishment in the Hereafter is the Fire.

And His saying: ﴿And Allah knows, while you do not know﴾, means: the innocence of ʿĀʾishah, and that He created her good and pure, free from indecencies.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And were it not for the grace of Allah upon you and His mercy, and that Allah is Kind and Merciful﴾. Its response clause (jawab, the apodosis of the conditional) is omitted, and its response is: "You would have been afflicted with the severe punishment immediately."

The Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 24, verse 21:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿O you who have believed, do not follow the steps of Satan﴾ — meaning: his misdeeds (khataya). It was also said: his traces (athar). It is said: his "stepping" (takhtiyuh) from the lawful to the unlawful, and from obedience to disobedience.

And His saying: ﴿And whoever follows the steps of Satan - indeed, he enjoins immorality﴾ — meaning: the ugly deeds (al-qaba'ih) of actions.

﴿And wrongdoing (al-munkar)﴾ — meaning: everything that Allah hates.

And His saying: ﴿And if not for the favor of Allah upon you and His mercy, not one of you would ever have been purified (zakka) — ever﴾ — meaning: no one among you would ever have become righteous (salaha).

﴿But Allah purifies whom He wills﴾ — meaning: He makes righteous whom He wills. The poet said:

(Indeed, we are like a spoiled thing... so when Allah sets it right, it becomes righteous.)

And His saying: ﴿And Allah is All-Hearing, All-Knowing﴾ — its meaning is clear.

The Almighty's words: ﴿And let not those of virtue and plenty among you swear off﴾ is derived from al-alyah (ألية), and al-alyah means oath. The poet said:

(Few are his oaths, guarding his oath... and if an oath slips from him, he fulfils it.)

The verse was revealed concerning Abu Bakr and Mistah. He was the cousin (ibn khala) of Abu Bakr and was dependent on his support, and he was a man of Badr among the earliest Emigrants. When he said what he said about A'ishah, God Almighty sent down her innocence from heaven, and Abu Bakr swore that he would not spend on him, and Mistah was a poor man with nothing. So God Almighty revealed this verse. It has also been read as "wa la yata'alli" (recited by Abu Ja'far). The majority hold that the meaning of His words ﴿and let not swear off﴾ is what we have explained. Others said its meaning is: "let them not fall short," from the saying of the speaker, "I do not fall short (la aluw) in your affair concerning such-and-such," i.e., I do not fall short. His words ﴿those of virtue and plenty among you﴾ mean: those of wealth and abundance.

His words ﴿that they should give to the near of kin, the needy, and the emigrants﴾ refer to Mistah, for he was a relative of Abu Bakr, was poor, and was one of the Emigrants. If someone asks: how is the singular mentioned with a plural form? We reply: such usage is permissible in the language, and it is possible that He meant him and others as well.

His words ﴿and let them pardon and overlook﴾ mean: let them pardon their deeds and overlook their words.

His words ﴿Do you not love that Allah should forgive you?﴾ are addressed to Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him. It is narrated that when this verse was revealed and recited to him, he said: "Yes, by Allah, we love that He should forgive us."

His words ﴿And Allah is Forgiving, Merciful﴾ mean: Concealing, Forgiving.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 24, verse 23:

The words of the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, those who accuse chaste, unwary, believing women﴾ — meaning: the unwary ones concerning immoral acts. Being unwary of immorality means that the act of immorality has not occurred in her heart. ʿĀʾishah, may Allah be pleased with her, was exactly like this.

As for His words: ﴿They are cursed in this world and the Hereafter﴾, it is related from Khuṣayf, who said: I said to Mujāhid: "Whoever accuses a believing woman, does Allah curse him in this world and the Hereafter?" He said: "That refers to ʿĀʾishah." And it is said: "This applies to all the wives of the Prophet."

As for His words: ﴿And for them is a great punishment﴾, we have already explained it.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 24, verse 24:

The Most High's saying: ﴿On the Day when their tongues, their hands and their feet will testify against them﴾ — the testimony of the tongues on the Day of Resurrection, by their speaking without the person's choice.

And His saying: ﴿their hands and their feet﴾ — it is said: their mouths will be sealed, then the hands and the feet will speak.

﴿for what they used to do﴾ — clear.

Allah's words, "On that Day Allah will pay them their full recompense, the Truth" (Qur'an 24:25): that is, their just reckoning.

And His words, "and they will know that Allah is the Truth, the Manifest" (Qur'an 24:25): that is, the Just, the One who manifests His justice.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 24, verse 26:

His statement, may He be exalted: ﴿Evil women are for evil men, and evil men for evil women; good women are for good men, and good men for good women﴾. There are two well-known opinions regarding this verse.

The first: evil words are for evil men, and evil men are for evil words; good and good words, and likewise.

The second opinion: evil women are for evil men, and evil men are for evil women; and likewise good women and good men. The evil man is ʿAbd Allah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul and those below him, and the evil women are his household. It is also said: his speech was about ʿĀʾisha, and the good women are ʿĀʾisha and women like her, and the good men are the Prophet (ﷺ) and his people.

Know that ʿĀʾisha (may Allah be pleased with her) used to take pride in several things, among them: that Jibril (peace be upon him) brought her image in a piece of silk (min) harir, meaning a piece of cloth, and said: "This is your wife." This was after the death of Khadija. It is also said that he brought her image in his palm. Among them: that the Prophet (ﷺ) did not marry a virgin except her. Among them: that the Prophet (ﷺ) died with his head in her lap and was buried in her house. Among them: that her innocence was revealed from the heavens. Among them: that she is the daughter of the Messenger of Allah's successor (khalifa), and that she is a sincere truthful woman (siddiqa).

Masruq, whenever he narrated from ʿĀʾisha, would say: "The truthful woman, daughter of the truthful one, the beloved of the Messenger of Allah, the one cleared from the heavens, related to me."

His statement: ﴿Those are cleared of what they say﴾, meaning: purified from what they say.

His statement: ﴿For them is forgiveness and generous provision﴾. Forgiveness is pardon for sins, and generous provision is Paradise.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 24, verse 27:

The Most High said: ﴿O you who have believed, do not enter houses other than your own houses until you have asked permission and greeted their occupants.﴾

Ibn 'Abbas recited: "until you seek permission" (hatta tastadhinu). He said: "tasta'nisu" (until you seek companionship/make yourselves known) is an error by the scribe; the well-known reading is "tasta'nisu." There are three opinions concerning it. The most famous is that "tastadhinu" means the same as "istidhan" (seeking permission). The second opinion is that it means clearing the throat (tanahnuh), as said by Mujahid. The third opinion is that "until you seek companionship" (hatta tasta'nisu) means becoming acquainted and inquiring, until one is given permission or is not given permission.

(27) ﴿But if you find no one in it, do not enter it until permission is given to you. And if it is said to you, "Go back," then go back.﴾

And His saying: ﴿and greet its occupants.﴾

The sunnah is that when a person reaches the door of a house, he says: "May I enter?" Some of them said: when the eye meets the eye, one precedes with the greeting, and when the eye does not meet the eye, one precedes with the seeking of permission.

It has been established from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "If one of you asks permission three times and is not given permission, let him return." It is related that Abu Musa al-Ash'ari came to the door of 'Umar, asked permission three times, was not granted permission, and returned. 'Umar said: "Did I not hear the voice of 'Abdullah ibn Qays?" They said: "He asked permission three times and returned." So he summoned him and said: "Why did you return?" He said: "I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say such-and-such." He said: "You must bring someone who will testify for you, or I will surely punish you with the whip (al-durra)." So Ubayy ibn Ka'b came and mentioned that to him, and he came and testified for him. It is also said that someone other than him testified for him.

Al-Hasan said: "The first (request) is an announcement (i'lam), the second is a consultation (mu'amara), and the third is a request for permission to return." It is related from Qatada that he said: "If permission is not given to him, he should not sit at the door, for people have needs." Some of them said: "If it is a public path, it is permissible for him to stand and sit; but if it is the courtyard of his house, he should not sit except with his permission." They said: "If the door is closed, one should not look at the house through a crack in the door; but if the door is open, there is no harm in looking, because when the door has been opened, permission has been given."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 24, verse 28:

And His Exalted saying: ﴿But if you find no one therein, do not enter until permission is given to you﴾ means: do not enter them without the permission of the owner.

And His saying: ﴿And if you are told, "Go back," then go back; it is purer for you﴾ means: if there are people in the house and they say, "Go back," then let him go back. The sunnah is that one should not alter the permission or the refusal, because the people may have excuses. Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him, would come to the door of an Ansari man to seek hadith. He would sit at the door until the man came out, without asking permission. The man would come out and say, "O cousin of the Messenger of Allah, would you not have informed me?" He would say, "This is how we have been commanded to seek knowledge."

And His saying: ﴿it is purer for you﴾ means: it is more beneficial for you (aslah lakum).

And His saying: ﴿And Allah is All-Knowing of what you do﴾ has an apparent meaning.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 24, verse 29:

His statement, exalted is He: ﴿There is no blame upon you for entering houses not inhabited⦆.

On this there are several opinions. The first: they are the lodgings along the road of travelers. The second opinion: they are the shops of merchants. The third opinion: they are the ruined houses. The fourth opinion: they are the caravanserais (khans) and lodgings on the roads, so entering them is for lodging and resting; as for the shops of merchants, the benefit in them is buying and selling; and as for the ruins, it is for urinating and defecating.

As for His statement: ﴿And Allah knows what you reveal and what you conceal⦆, its meaning is apparent.

It is narrated from Shu'ayb ibn al-Hubhab, who said: Abu al-'Aliyah used to come to me while I was in my shop (dukkan), and he would ask permission and then enter. I would say to him: "It is only a shop (hanut)." He would say to me: "A person is alone in his shop with his accounts and his dirhams."

As for seeking permission before entering upon those within the forbidden degrees (mahram), if they are in a separate house, one asks permission; and if they are in one house, then when he enters upon them he should clear his throat and make some slight movement.

It was said to Qatadah: "Shall I not ask permission before entering upon my mother?" He said: "Would you like to see her private parts?" He said: "No." He said: "Then ask permission."

It is narrated from Ibrahim al-Nakha'i that he said: "There is no need for permission for the shops of the market."

It is narrated from Ibn Sirin that whenever he came to a shop in the market, he would say: "Peace be upon you, may I enter?" Then he would enter.

It is narrated from Abu Musa al-Ash'ari and Hudhayfah that he would ask permission before entering upon those within the forbidden degrees, and similarly from al-Hasan al-Basri.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 24, verse 30:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Tell the believing men to lower their gaze﴾ — the verse. "Min" is extra (ṣila), and its meaning is: lower their gazes. This was related from Sa'id ibn Jubayr. Some of them said: "min" here is for partitive (tab'id), and it is mentioned here because lowering the gaze is obligatory only regarding what is forbidden, and not obligatory regarding what is permitted.

And His saying: ﴿and guard their private parts﴾ — this is a command to chastity (ta'affuf). Abu al-'Aliyah said: guarding the private parts throughout the whole Qur'an carries the meaning of refraining from what is forbidden, but here it carries the meaning of concealing (satr).

It has been related from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said to 'Ali (may Allah be pleased with him): "Indeed you have a treasure in Paradise, and you are the lord of its two horns (dhu qarnayha), so do not follow a glance with a glance; for the first is yours, and the second is against you." Narrated by Ahmad ibn Hanbal in his Musnad? [translation note: the text reads "رَوَاهُ على نَفسه"; rendered literally below]

Narrated by ['Ali] himself. And from some of the early generations (salaf) he said: "Indeed, the gaze plants desire in the heart, and many a desire has left a long grief." And from Khalid ibn Abi 'Imran that he said: "Indeed a man may look a single look and his heart is pierced, just as the hide is pierced, so his heart becomes corrupt until it no longer benefits from it."

Abu Umamah related from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "Whoever looks at the beauty of a woman and lowers his gaze, [reciting] ﴿And tell the believing women to lower their gaze, and guard their private parts, and not display their adornment except what appears thereof﴾ — Allah will give him a worship whose sweetness he will find."

And His saying: ﴿That is purer for them﴾ — i.e., more pure for them.

And His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah is Acquainted with what they do﴾ — i.e., Knowing of what they do.

**Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 24, verse 31:**

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And say to the believing women that they should lower their gaze and guard their private parts.﴾

It is narrated that Ibn Umm Maktum came to the Prophet while Umm Salamah and Maymunah were with him. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to them: "Veil yourselves." They said: "He is blind." He said: "Are you two blind as well?"

His words: ﴿And not display their adornment.﴾ The adornment (zinah) is everything with which a woman adorns herself, such as jewelry and garments.

His words: ﴿except what appears thereof.﴾ Opinions differ on this. Ibn Mas'ud said: it refers to garments. This is the view chosen by Abu 'Ubayd.

The second view is what is related from Ibn 'Abbas, that he said: it is kohl. al-Kalbi related from him that he said: it is kohl, the ring and dyeing (khidab). He also said: it is the face and the two palms. Know that the intended meaning of adornment here, in the words ﴿and let them draw their khimar (headcovers) over their juyub (chests/necklines), and not display their adornment except to their husbands, or their fathers, or the fathers of their husbands, or their sons, or the sons of their husbands, or their brothers, or the sons of their brothers, or the sons of﴾, is the place of adornment. Based on this, it is permissible to look at a woman's face and palms without desire, and if one fears desire, one must lower the gaze.

Know that adornment is of two kinds: outward adornment and inward adornment. Outward adornment is kohl, the ring (fatkhah), and dyeing when it is on the palm. As for dyeing on the foot, it is inward adornment. As for the bracelet on the arm, 'A'ishah said it is outward adornment, but the more correct view is that it is inward adornment, and this is the view of most scholars. As for the armlet (dumluj), the necklace (mukhanaqah), the pendant, and similar items, these are inward adornment. Therefore, what is outward adornment may be looked at by a non-mahram without desire, while what is inward adornment may not be looked at by a non-mahram. As for the husband, he may look and enjoy. As for the mahrams, they may look without enjoyment.

His words: ﴿and let them draw their khimar over their juyub.﴾ That is, let them draw their coverings over their chests. At that time, women used to let their headcovers fall down their backs, so their chests and necks were exposed. Allah the Exalted therefore commanded them to draw their coverings over their chests, so that their chests and necks would not be seen. Safiyyah bint Shaybah related from 'A'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her, that when this verse was revealed, the women of the Ansar went to the edges of their waistcloths, cut a piece from them, and covered themselves with it. In the morning, it was as if there were crows upon their heads.

His words: ﴿and not display their adornment.﴾ The intended meaning of this adornment is the inward adornment.

His words: ﴿except to their husbands.﴾ That is, their spouses.

His words: ﴿or their fathers, or the fathers of their husbands, or their sons, or the sons of their husbands, or their brothers, or the sons of their brothers, or the sons of their sisters.﴾ It is permissible for these people to look at the inward adornment, except that they may not look at what lies between the navel and the knee. It is lawful for the husband to look at all of it. As for the private part itself, there are two opinions on it, as is known in fiqh (jurisprudence). It has been related from 'A'ishah what indicates that looking at the private part is disliked, and it has been said that it causes blindness.

His words: ﴿or their women.﴾ On this there are two opinions. The first: the intended meaning is Muslim women. Based on this, it is not permissible for a Muslim woman to reveal her beauty before a Jewish or Christian woman.

The second opinion: the words ﴿their women﴾ are general to all women. Therefore, a woman may look at another woman, except for what lies between the navel and the knee.

His words: ﴿or what their right hands possess.﴾ Opinions differ on this. It has been related from 'A'ishah and Umm Salamah that they said: the intended meaning is slaves. Accordingly, a male slave may look at his female owner in the same way a close relative (dhu rahim) looks, without desire, and this applies when the slave is chaste. The second opinion is that of Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib and a group of the Successors (tabi'un), who said: a male slave may not look at his female owner except in the way a non-mahram looks at a non-mahram. Based on this, the verse is understood as referring to female slaves. The first opinion is more evident in the meaning of the verse, because the words ﴿or their women﴾ have already preceded, and so they include free women and slave women. There is a third opinion regarding the verse: that a male slave may look at his female owner at what appears during work and service, such as the forearms, the feet, and the neck, but not at anything beyond that. This is permitted because it is difficult to cover this in front of slaves, whereas it is not difficult in front of non-mahrams. It is related from Umm Salamah, may Allah be pleased with her, that she made a contract of manumission (kitabah) with a slave of hers called Nabhan, and she would not veil herself from him. Then one day she said to him: "O Nabhan, how much remains of your contract?" He said: "Two thousand dirhams." She said: "Pay it to Muhammad ibn 'Abdullah ibn Abi Umayyah, and peace be upon you," and she removed her veil.

His words: ﴿or the attendant men who have no physical desire (ghayr uli al-irbah).﴾ Opinions differ on this. Mujahid said: they are the men or the boys who have not attained awareness of women's private matters. Ikrimah said: they are the impotent man (al-'unnin). Some said: they are the decrepit old man. It is related from some that they are the castrated man (al-majbub). It is well known in the tafsir literature that they are those who follow men and have no concern except their stomachs, and who do not understand matters concerning women. It is said that this refers to the effeminate man (mukhannath) who has no need for women. It is related from 'A'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her, that an effeminate man named Hit used to enter upon the wives of the Prophet. She said: "We used to think that he was one of those without physical desire," meaning that he did not understand anything about women. One day he described a woman, saying: "She turns toward you with four (folds) and turns away with eight." The Prophet heard this and said: "I did not think he understood this," and he ordered that he be expelled.

As for irbah, it means need, derived from irb. From this is the hadith of 'A'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her, that "the Prophet used to kiss while fasting, and he was the one who controlled his desire (akmalakum li-irbihi)." Whoever says otherwise has erred.

His words: ﴿or the children who have not attained awareness of women's private parts.﴾ That is, the children who have not attained this awareness. The singular is used here with the meaning of the plural.

His words: ﴿who have not attained awareness of women's private parts.﴾ That is, they have not yet become capable of understanding women's matters. It is also said: "they have not attained awareness of women's private parts," meaning they do not know the private parts apart from other parts, so they cannot distinguish. It is said: they have not reached the age of desire.

His words: ﴿and let them not strike their feet so that what they conceal of their adornment may be known.﴾ It is related that a woman would pass by men while she had an anklet on her foot, and she would strike her foot so that they would hear the sound of her anklet. Therefore, they were forbidden from this. If someone asks: what is wrong with striking the anklet that would necessitate prohibition? The answer: it involves soliciting inclination and stirring desire.

His words: ﴿And turn to Allah in repentance all together, O believers.﴾ On this there are two opinions. The first: the intended meaning is repentance from minor sins, because lapses (lamam) occur among all believers; minor sins occur among all believers, but major sins do not. Others said: no, rather the verse is general to both minor and major sins. Repentance is remorse for what has passed, ceasing the sin immediately, and resolve not to return to it. This is the meaning of sincere repentance (nasuh) mentioned in other passages. Some mentioned that Allah the Exalted commanded the polytheists to repent absolutely, saying: ﴿Say to those who disbelieve: if they desist, what has passed will be forgiven for them.﴾ He commanded the Jews and Christians to repent, to reform, and to clarify, which is the clarification of the description of the Prophet, saying: ﴿except those who repent, reform, and make clear.﴾ He commanded the hypocrites to repent, reform, hold fast to Allah, and make their religion sincerely for Allah, saying: ﴿except those who repent, reform, hold fast to Allah, and make their religion sincerely for Allah.﴾ The meaning of this has been explained before. In this verse, He commanded all believers to repent, and every person must repent, whether from a minor or a major sin. It has been established through the narration of al-Aghar al-Muzani that the Prophet said: "O people, repent to Allah, for I repent to Him a hundred times every day." Muslim recorded it in his Sahih.

﴿among you, and the righteous among your male and female slaves. If they are poor, Allah will enrich them from His bounty.﴾

His words: ﴿so that you may prosper.﴾ That is, that you may be happy and succeed.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 24, verse 32:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And marry off the unmarried among you﴾. That is: marry off the unmarried women (al-ayama) among you. The ayim is the name for every woman who has no husband, whether she is a thayyib (previously married) or a virgin (bikr). The poet said:

(So if you marry, I will marry; and if you remain unmarried... for all time, as long as you do not marry, I will remain unmarried.)

Dawud (al-Zahiri) and the companions of the literalist school (ashab al-Zahir) held that marriage is obligatory, and they used this verse as evidence. As for us, it is permissible (mubah) at one time and recommended (sunnah) at another: it is permissible when a man's self does not long for women, and recommended when his self longs for women. It has been narrated from the Prophet that he said: "Whoever loves my fitrah (natural disposition), let him follow my sunnah, and among my sunnah is marriage."

It is established from the Prophet that he said: "Whoever among you is able to bear the expenses (al-ba'ah) of marriage, let him marry, for it is more effective in lowering the gaze and more protective of the private parts. And whoever is not able, let him fast, for fasting is a shield for him."

It is related from some of the early generation (al-salaf) that he said: Whoever is overcome by desire and has wealth, let him marry; and if he has no wealth, let him look often at the sky, for his desire will go away.

His saying: ﴿And the righteous among your male slaves and your female slaves﴾.

It was recited in the irregular (shadhdh) reading: "from your male slaves (min 'abidikum) and your female slaves." Marry off the unmarried from among the free women, and marry off the righteous from among the male and female slaves. The meaning of "ibad" here is the slaves (al-'abid).

His saying: ﴿If they are poor, Allah will enrich them from His bounty﴾. It is narrated from Umar that he said: I am amazed at whoever seeks wealth without marriage, while Allah, Exalted, says: ﴿If they are poor, Allah will enrich them from His bounty﴾. And from some of them: Allah, Exalted, promised wealth through marriage and promised wealth through separation. He said regarding marriage: ﴿Allah will enrich them from His bounty﴾, meaning: from Allah; and He said regarding separation: ﴿But if they separate, Allah will enrich each of them from His abundance﴾. It is said that the wealth here is the wealth of contentment (qana'ah). It is also said: it is the combining of two livelihoods. And it is said regarding His saying: ﴿And He found you poor and enriched you﴾, that it means: through the wealth of Khadijah.

His saying: ﴿And Allah is All-Encompassing, All-Knowing﴾, meaning: abundant in wealth, knowing of the states of the servants. It is narrated from al-Hasan ibn Ali, may Allah be pleased with them both, that he used to marry and divorce often, and he would say: "I only seek wealth through marriage and divorce," and he would recite these two verses. Some of them have mentioned that the ayim, just as it applies to a woman, applies to a man: it is said "a man is ayim" if he has no wife, and "a woman is ayim" if she has no husband. The poetry we recited is evidence for this. In a report: "The Prophet forbade the ayimah," meaning: the one who is unmarried (al-'azbah).

It is narrated from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad that he said: We were commanded to kill the ayim, meaning: the living (al-hayyah). Some of them said: ﴿And marry off the unmarried among you and the righteous﴾ means: with the righteous. His saying: ﴿from your servants﴾ means: from your men. Then He commanded afterwards the marrying of the female slaves. The first opinion mentioned earlier is the most apparent.

His saying: ﴿And let those who find no means of marriage keep themselves chaste﴾ means: let those who do not find what they could marry with seek chastity.

His saying: ﴿until Allah enriches them from His bounty﴾ has two meanings. The first is that they find wealth with which they are able to marry. The second is that Allah grants them the ability to be patient and refrain from marriage. It is related from Ikrimah that he said: if a man sees a woman and desires her, then if he has a wife, let him go to her; and if he has no wife, let him reflect on the dominion of the heavens and the earth.

﴿So make a contract of manumission (kitabah) with them, if you know any good in them﴾

His saying: ﴿And those who seek a deed of manumission (al-kitab) from among those whom your right hands possess﴾ means: those who seek a contract of manumission (kitabah) from among those whom your right hands possess, that is, from the male and female slaves. Kitabah is that a master enters into a contract with his slave for a sum of money on the condition that, when he pays it, he is freed. The occasion of revelation of this verse was that Huwaytib ibn Abd al-Uzza had a slave, who asked him to make a contract of manumission with him, but he refused, so Allah the Exalted revealed this verse.

His saying: ﴿So make a contract with them﴾: most scholars hold that it is a command of recommendation, not of obligation. A group held that it is a command of obligation if the slave has money with which to pay. Abu Muhammad ibn Sirin related: he was a slave of Anas ibn Malik, and asked Anas to make a contract of manumission with him, but Anas refused. Ibn Sirin mentioned that to Umar, and Umar said to Anas: make a contract with him. He refused, so Umar struck him with a whip (dirra) until he made the contract. Ibn Jurayj said: I asked Ata: must a master make a contract of manumission with his slave if he asks? He said: yes. The same is related from al-Dahhak, who said: this applies when there is money at the time of the contract; if there is no money, it is not obligatory. It is also related that a slave of Salman said to him: make a contract with me. He said: do you have money? He said: no. He said: do you want to feed me the filth of people? And he did not make a contract with him.

His saying: ﴿if you know any good in them﴾ means wealth. This was said by Ibn Abbas. Similar is His saying: ﴿And indeed he is intense in his love of good﴾, meaning love of wealth. The poet said:

"What do souls hope for from seeking good, and from love of life, when its bearer is struck?"

meaning wealth. Al-Hasan al-Basri said: ﴿if you know any good in them﴾ means religion. ﴿And give them of the wealth of Allah which He has given you. And do not compel your slave girls to prostitution if they desire chastity, in order to seek the transient goods of worldly life﴾, and trustworthiness. Al-Nakha'i said: fidelity and truthfulness. It is related from some of them: capacity to earn wealth.

Al-Zajjaj said: had He meant by "good" wealth, He would have said: "if you know good for them." When He said: ﴿in them, any good﴾, it shows that He meant fidelity and truthfulness.

His saying: ﴿And give them of the wealth of Allah which He has given you﴾ has several views. Abd Allah ibn Buraydah related from his father that he said: it is an urging of people to help those who make contracts of manumission. According to this, the verse includes both the master and others.

The second view is that it refers to the share of slaves (riqab), since Allah has assigned a share to those in contracts of manumission among the alms. The third view is that His saying ﴿And give them﴾ is addressed specifically to the masters.

His saying: ﴿of the wealth of Allah which He has given you﴾ refers to the payment of the contract. This was related from Uthman, Ali and al-Zubayr. Then they differed. Some said: help him with the money of the contract. Others said: reduce from him some of the money of the contract. It is related from Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, that he reduces a quarter of it; from Ibn Abbas that he reduces a third of it; and from some of them that he reduces some amount without specifying it. This is the view of al-Shafi'i. They also differed as to whether this is by way of recommendation or obligation. According to some of the Companions we mentioned, it is recommendation, and according to others it is obligatory, and obligation is more apparent.

His saying: ﴿And do not compel your slave girls to prostitution﴾ means to fornication. The verse was revealed concerning Abd Allah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul and a group of hypocrites, who used to compel their slave girls to fornication in order to obtain earnings. It is related that Abd Allah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul had a slave girl called Mathla, whom he ordered to fornicate, so she brought a cloak. Then he ordered her again, and she refused, so Allah the Exalted revealed this verse.

His saying: ﴿if they desire chastity﴾ means desire to keep chaste. If it is said: does the verse imply that if they do not desire chastity, it is permissible to compel them to fornication? The answer has two parts. The first is that He mentioned ﴿if they desire chastity﴾ because compulsion occurs only in this situation; if they do not desire chastity, they commit fornication willingly.

The second answer is that ﴿if they desire chastity﴾ relates to the preceding verse, namely His saying: ﴿And marry the unmarried among you and the righteous among your male and female slaves﴾, if they desire chastity.

His saying: ﴿in order to seek the transient goods of worldly life﴾ means: in order to seek the wealth of this world. In some reports: "The world is a present possession, from which the righteous and the wicked eat, while the Hereafter is a true promise, in which a powerful King judges. So be among the children of the Hereafter, and do not be among the children of this world."

His saying: ﴿And whoever compels them, then indeed Allah, after their compulsion, is Forgiving and Merciful﴾ means: to them. Thus it was related in the recitation of Ibn Abbas: "then indeed Allah, after their compulsion, is to them Forgiving and Merciful."

The Exalted's saying: ﴿Indeed We have sent down to you clear verses﴾ means: [clear] concerning the lawful (ḥalāl) and the unlawful (ḥarām). His saying: ﴿clear﴾ means: evident, with no ambiguity in them.

His saying: ﴿and an example from those who passed away before you﴾ means: a comparison of your situation with theirs, so that you do not do what they did, lest there befall you what befell them.

His saying: ﴿and an admonition for the God-fearing﴾ means: a reminder and a warning.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 24, verse 35:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Allah is the Light of the heavens and the earth.﴾ Ibn ʿAbbas said: He is the guide of the people of the heavens and the earth. (And it is also related from him that he said: the illumination of the heavens and the earth.) And it is related from Qatadah and others: the one who gives light to the heavens and the earth. It is said: the light of the heavens is by the angels, and the earth by the prophets. It is also said: the light of the heavens is by the stars, the sun and the moon, and the light of the earth by plants and flowers.

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿The likeness of His light﴾. Ubayy ibn Kaʿb recited: "the likeness of the light of the believer." And it is related from Ibn Masʿud that he recited: "the likeness of His light in the heart of the believer." (It is well known that ﴿the likeness of His light﴾ has several opinions, including: ﴿The heavens and the earth—the likeness of His light is like a niche in which is a lamp, the lamp within glass, the glass as though it were a brilliant star﴾.) The first: its meaning is: the likeness of the light of God in the heart of the believer, which is the light by which one is guided, and this is in the sense of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿So he is upon a light from his Lord﴾. The second opinion: ﴿the likeness of His light﴾, i.e., the light of the believer's heart through faith. The third opinion: that it is the light of Muhammad. Some interpreted it as referring to the Qur'an.

His saying: ﴿like a niche﴾. The mishkat is the recess that has no opening. Some said: the mishkat is the iron piece on which the lamp is hung, which is the chain. It was also said: the place in which the wick is placed, which is like a tube. The first is the most apparent and preferable of the opinions. The meaning of mishkat here is: the chest, as said by Ubayy ibn Kaʿb. His saying: ﴿in it is a lamp﴾, i.e., a flame of fire.

His saying: ﴿the lamp within glass﴾. Glass (zujajah) is a known thing; it is a substance that has brightness. If it is asked: why was glass specifically mentioned? We say: Ubayy ibn Kaʿb said: the niche is the chest, the glass is the heart, and the lamp is faith. So He mentioned the glass because the lamp within it has radiance. Some others said: He mentioned the glass because when it breaks, nothing benefits from it; likewise the heart, when it is corrupted, nothing benefits from it.

His saying: ﴿the glass as though it were a brilliant star﴾. He likened the glass to a star. Some said: this star is Venus, for it is the brightest star in the sky. Others said: the five planets are Saturn, Jupiter, Mars, Mercury and Venus. If it is asked: why was it not likened to the sun and the moon? We say: because the sun and the moon are subject to eclipse, while the stars are not subject to eclipse. As for His saying: ﴿durriyy﴾ (brilliant), it is attributed to durr (pearl), and it is attributed to pearl because of its purity and its color. It was read as "durri'" with a kasra on the dal, a hamza and a madd. There are two opinions regarding it: the first is that it is derived from al-dara', which is repelling, and the star repels the devils from the heaven. If it is asked: why was it likened to it in the state of repelling? We say: because in that state it is purest. The second opinion: "durri'," meaning rising; it is said: "daraʾa ʿalayna fulan," meaning he rose and appeared. Al-Azhari said: this is a good opinion. It was also read as "durri'" with a damma on the dal, hamzated, which Hamzah and Abu Bakr recited, and the grammarians err in this reading, saying: fa'il does not occur in the language. The anomalous reading is "durri" with a fatha on the dal.

His saying: ﴿it is lit﴾, i.e., the glass; its meaning is: the fire of the glass, so the word "fire" is omitted. It was read as "yūqad" with the yā', i.e., the lamp; it was read as "tawaqqad," i.e., it blazes. In the anomalous reading: "yūqad," i.e., Allah the Exalted kindles it.

His saying: ﴿from a blessed tree﴾, i.e., from the oil of a blessed tree. The blessed tree here is the olive, and it contains good that is not in other trees, for it is oil, condiment and fruit that is eaten, and it is used for lighting, and by its virtue clothes are washed with it. It is a tree that is green from its top to its bottom, and extracting its oil does not require a press as other trees do; rather, one extracts it with ease whoever wishes. It has been related from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "Eat with olive oil and anoint yourselves with it, for it is from a blessed tree," narrated by Mamar, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from his father, from ʿUmar, the report.

His saying: ﴿neither eastern nor western﴾. Al-Hasan said: this is not one of the trees of this world; had it been one of the trees of this world, it would have been eastern or western. Others said: rather, it is a description of the olive—and this is the most correct. There are opinions on it. The first: its meaning is: not eastern, i.e., it is not one that the sun shines upon at sunrise only, nor one that the sun sets upon only, so that it would be neither eastern nor western.

His saying: ﴿nor western﴾, i.e., it is not one that the sun sets upon and does not shine upon, so that it would be neither western nor eastern. The meaning of the verse is that it is not purely of the east, nor purely of the west, but rather it is eastern-western, meaning between east and west, neither purely of the east nor purely of the west, and the sun shines upon it at all times. When that is so, its oil is brighter. They said: this is like saying: so-and-so is neither black nor white, i.e., he is not purely black nor purely white, that is, black and white are combined in him. And it is said: this pomegranate is neither sweet nor sour, i.e., sweetness and sourness are combined in it and it is not purely one of them. This is the view of al-Farra', al-Zajjaj and most of the scholars of meanings. Ibn Qutaybah claimed that the meaning of His saying ﴿neither eastern nor western﴾ is: it is not in a sunny spot, nor in a shaded spot; i.e., it is not in a sunny spot so that the sun is always upon it, nor in shade so that it is always in shade. The third opinion: it is a tree among trees, neither exposed to the sun at its rising nor exposed to it at its setting.

His saying: ﴿its oil would almost glow﴾, i.e., because of its purity and its color.

His saying: ﴿even if no fire touched it﴾, i.e., even if no fire touched it.

His saying: ﴿light upon light﴾, i.e., the light of the lamp upon the light of the glass.

His saying: ﴿Allah guides to His light whom He wills﴾, i.e., the light of insight and conviction.

His saying: ﴿And Allah presents parables for the people﴾, i.e., Allah makes the parables clear to the people.

His saying: ﴿And Allah is Knowing of all things﴾ is well known.

Know that opinions differ regarding the meaning of the parable. Some said: the parable refers to the light in the heart of the believer; some said: the parable refers to the light of Muhammad; and some said: the parable refers to the light of the Qur'an. As for when we say that the parable refers to the light in the heart of the believer, its meaning is apparent, as we have explained.

His saying: ﴿its oil would almost glow﴾, i.e., the heart of the believer almost recognizes the truth before it is made clear to it, because it agrees with it.

His saying: ﴿light upon light﴾, i.e., the light of action upon the light of belief. It is related from Ubayy ibn Kaʿb that he said: the believer is between five lights: his speech is a light, his action is a light, his entrance is a light, his exit is a light, and his destination is toward the light. It is related from another that he said: the believer is between four states: if he is given, he is thankful; if he is tested, he is patient; if he speaks, he is truthful; and if he judges, he is just. When we say that the parable refers to the light of Muhammad, then the niche is his chest, the glass is his heart, and the lamp is the light of prophethood.

His saying: ﴿kindled from a blessed tree﴾: the blessed tree is Ibrahim (peace be upon him), and the olive is mentioned because it is the most blessed of trees, as we have explained; and because Ibrahim settled in Syria, and the olives of Syria have a blessing that no other land has.

His saying: ﴿neither eastern nor western﴾ means that Ibrahim did not pray toward the east nor toward the west, and this is the meaning of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Ibrahim was neither a Jew nor a Christian﴾, for the Jews pray toward the west and the Christians toward the east.

His saying: ﴿its oil would almost glow, even if no fire touched it﴾ means: even if Ibrahim had not been a prophet, Allah would have joined him, by his good deeds, with the prophets in their ranks. It is also said that its meaning is: even if no miracle had come to Muhammad, his circumstances would have indicated his truthfulness and his prophethood.

His saying: ﴿light upon light﴾, i.e., the light of Muhammad upon the light of Ibrahim.

His saying: {Allah guides to His light whom He wills}, meaning: Allah guides to belief in Muhammad whom He wills. All of this is the meaning of what al-Dahhak related from Ibn ʿAbbas. There is much discussion regarding the verse, which those who deal with spiritual insights mention, but it is not occupied with it, and these two opinions are the well-known ones.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 24, verse 36:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿In houses which Allah has permitted to be raised﴾ means: lit (tawqid) in houses. It is also said: the lamps are in houses, and the houses here are the mosques. As for His saying ﴿Allah has permitted to be raised﴾, there are several opinions. Mujahid said: built. Al-Hasan said: exalted. That is, that frivolous speech is not mentioned in them. And it is reported from some of them: purified.

His saying ﴿and His name is mentioned therein﴾ has an apparent meaning.

His saying ﴿glorified﴾ (yusabbihu). It has been read as "yusabbaha" with a kasra on the ba', so that his saying with a kasra on the ba' means: men glorify (yusabbihu rijal). His saying "yusabbihu" with a fatha is in the passive form, the subject unnamed. The meaning of yusabbihu is: prays (yusalli).

His saying ﴿in the mornings and the evenings﴾ means: at dawn and at dusk. The poet said:

(I stood there at the time of asil, not asking it, / it was unable to answer, and there was no one in the abode.)

He specified the morning and the afternoon only because the dawn prayer and the afternoon prayer were the first to be made obligatory upon the Muslims. It is reported from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, that he said: The Duha prayer is in the Qur'an, and the divers do not dive for it. Then he recited this verse, which is His saying ﴿in the mornings and the evenings﴾, and he claimed that the intended glorification in the morning is the Duha prayer. The well-known view is what we have explained, namely that what is intended by it is the dawn prayer and the afternoon prayer.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 24, verse 37:

The Exalted's saying: ﴿Men whom neither commerce nor sale distracts from the remembrance of Allah﴾. It is related from ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr that he said: On the Day of Resurrection, Allah will place pulpits of light, and He will say: "Where are those whom neither commerce nor sale distracted from the remembrance of Allah?" They will stand up, and He will seat them upon them.

Al-Farrāʾ (the grammarian) said: "Tijāra (commerce) is what is sold from imported goods (al-jalb), and bayʿ (sale) is what you sell with your own hand."

And His saying: ﴿and the establishment of prayer﴾. If it is said: "If you interpret the remembrance of Allah as the five daily prayers, what is the meaning of His saying ﴿and the establishment of prayer﴾?" We say: its meaning is guarding the appointed times (mawāqīt), and whoever does not guard the appointed times has not established the prayer. And His saying ﴿wa-iqām al-ṣalāh﴾ means "wa-iqāmat al-ṣalāh" (and the establishing of the prayer), so the ʾalif of the feminine (tāʾ marbūṭa) has been dropped by the rule of the construct (idāfa). The poet said:

(Indeed the companions have hastened the separation and departed, and they have broken to you the promise they made...)

That is, ʿiddat al-umūr (the number of matters).

And His saying ﴿and the giving of zakāt﴾: some said it is the obligatory zakāt, and others said it is the righteous deeds.

And His saying ﴿they fear a Day when hearts and eyes will be turned about﴾, meaning: the hearts will turn from what they were upon in the world of doubt and disbelief, and the eyes will be opened from their coverings.
