It is also said: the heart turns between fear and hope, for it fears destruction and hopes for salvation. As for the turning of the sight, until it looks from where its record will be given, from its left or from its right. And he said: the hearts turn in the chest, rising up to the throat, so they neither leave nor depart; and as for the turning of the sight, it is its fixed staring from the terror and severity of the matter.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 24, verse 38:

And His saying: ﴿That Allah may reward them with the best of what they did﴾ means: that He may reward them for the good deeds they did.

And His saying: ﴿and increase them from His bounty﴾ means: an increase beyond what they deserve.

And His saying: ﴿And Allah provides for whom He wills without reckoning﴾ — we have already explained it.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 24, verse 39:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And those who disbelieve, their deeds are﴾. Know that when Allah, the Exalted, mentioned the parable concerning the believers, He followed it with a parable concerning the disbelievers.

His saying: ﴿like a mirage﴾. The sarab (mirage) is what one sees at midday, resembling flowing water over the ground, and what is most often seen by the thirsty one. Al-Farra' said: the sarab is what clings to the ground, and the al (mirage-haze) is what rises up from the ground; it is a shimmer between the sky and the earth, resembling a sheet, in which the small appears large and the short appears tall.

Another said: the sarab is at midday, the al in the early morning, and the raqraq in the evenings. The poet said:

(When we restrained the war, their covenants were like the gleam of a mirage glittering in the desert.)

His saying: ﴿in a valley (qi'ah)﴾. The qa' is the flat, level land.

His saying: ﴿until, when he comes to it, he finds it to be nothing﴾, meaning: he does not find in it anything of what he hoped for and reckoned.

His saying: ﴿but he finds Allah with him﴾, meaning: with His knowledge; its meaning is that he meets Allah in the Hereafter.

﴿Then He pays him his account in full﴾, meaning: the recompense for his deeds. The poet said:

(He turned away fleeing, rushing headlong, and knew that he would encounter the reckoning.)

His saying: ﴿And Allah is swift in reckoning﴾, whose meaning is clear.

Know that concerning the revelation of this verse there are two views. The first: it was revealed concerning Shayba ibn Rabi'a, who used to seek religion before the Prophet was sent; he would wear wool and eat barley, then when the Prophet was sent he disbelieved in him.

The second view: the verse was revealed concerning all the disbelievers, and the purpose of the verse is to liken their deeds to a mirage. Their deeds are what they believed to be good, such as the Hajj, maintaining ties of kinship, good treatment of neighbours, hospitality to guests, fulfilling covenants, and what is similar to these. Allah, the Exalted, mentioned that these deeds are like a mirage, since they do not proceed from a believer; he hopes for good and reward from them, and when he reaches them his expectation deceives him, and he obtains nothing.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 24, verse 40:

The words of His, the Exalted: ﴿Or like darkness in a deep sea (bahr lujji)﴾. The scholars of meanings (ahl al-ma'ani) said: the meaning of the verse is that if you liken their deeds to what is found (to a mirage), then it is as we have explained, like a mirage in a level plain (qay'a); and if you liken their deeds to what is seen, then it is like darkness in the deep sea. The deep sea (al-bahr al-lujji) is the profound one whose depth is deep. In a report, the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Whoever rides the sea when it is in its depths (hina yalij), the dhimma (protection of Allah and His Messenger) has been removed from him."

Its meaning: when he goes into the middle of the sea and reaches its deepest point. As for the darknesses (zulumat): they are the darkness of the sea, the darkness of the night, the darkness of the clouds, and also the darkness of the waves.

His words: ﴿Covered by waves, above which are waves, above which is cloud﴾ — this is the darknesses we have mentioned.

His words: ﴿Darknesses, one above another﴾ — meaning: the darkness of the wave upon the darkness of the sea, and the darkness of the cloud upon the darkness of the wave.

His words: ﴿If he brings out his hand, he can hardly see it﴾ — that is, he has not seen it. It was said: he did not come close to seeing it. It is said: the word "yakad" (can hardly) here is a connective particle (silah). The poet said:

(And when its brightness is raised, / none sees its light except the seeing one)

His words: ﴿And whomever Allah does not give light, for him there is no light﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said its meaning: whomever Allah does not make a religion (din) for, for him there is no religion. It is also said its meaning: whomever Allah does not guide, no one can guide him.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 24, verses 41–42:

And His saying: ﴿Have you not seen that to Allah glorifies whoever is in the heavens and the earth?﴾ We have already explained it.

And His saying: ﴿And the birds in flight﴾ means: in rows (ṣāffāt), the wings being spread out.

And His saying: ﴿Each has known its prayer and its glorification﴾. Mujāhid said: the prayer (ṣalāh) belongs to human beings, and the glorification (tasbīḥ) belongs to all of creation. It is also said: the beating of the wings is the prayer of the bird, and its sound is its glorification.

And His saying: ﴿And Allah is Knowing of what they do﴾ — its meaning is clear. Likewise His saying: ﴿And to Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth, and to Allah is the final return﴾.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 24, verses 41–42:

And His saying: ﴿Have you not seen that to Allah glorifies whoever is in the heavens and the earth?﴾ We have already explained it.

And His saying: ﴿And the birds in flight﴾ means: in rows (ṣāffāt), the wings being spread out.

And His saying: ﴿Each has known its prayer and its glorification﴾. Mujāhid said: the prayer (ṣalāh) belongs to human beings, and the glorification (tasbīḥ) belongs to all of creation. It is also said: the beating of the wings is the prayer of the bird, and its sound is its glorification.

And His saying: ﴿And Allah is Knowing of what they do﴾ — its meaning is clear. Likewise His saying: ﴿And to Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth, and to Allah is the final return﴾.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 24, verse 43:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Have you not seen that Allah drives the clouds﴾ means: drives the clouds along. The poet said:

(Indeed I have come to you from my land and my homeland... driving the last breath of a soul that has scarcely any life left in it.)

And His saying: ﴿then joins them together﴾ means: gathers them together.

And His saying: ﴿then makes them into a heap﴾ means: piled up, some of it upon others.

And His saying: ﴿then you see the rain come out from within it﴾ means: the rain comes out from within it. The khilal (gaps, openings) is the plural of khalal, as jibal (mountains) is the plural of jabal. The poet said regarding the rain (wadq):

(Neither a cloud has poured its rain... nor a land has been made green by its greening.)

And His saying: ﴿And He sends down from the sky mountains [of hail] wherein is hail﴾ it is narrated from Ibn 'Abbas that he said: In the sky there are mountains of hail, and hail is sent down from them.

Ibn 'Abbas said: He addressed the people in terms they would recognize; otherwise, snow is more than hail, but the Arabs had never seen snow. And it is narrated from Ibn 'Abbas that he said: Snow is a white thing that descends from the sky; I have never seen it. Others said: His saying: ﴿and He sends down from the sky mountains﴾ means: an amount equal to mountains in quantity, and it is said: so-and-so has mountains of wealth, likened to mountains for abundance.

His saying: ﴿min﴾ is a connecting particle (silah); its meaning is: He sends down from the sky mountains ﴿of hail﴾.

His saying: ﴿so He strikes with it whom He wills﴾ means: He strikes with the hail whom He wills, ﴿and averts it from whom He wills﴾.

His saying: ﴿The flash of its lightning nearly takes away the sight﴾ means: the light of its lightning (sana barqihi). We have already cited poetry on this.

His saying: ﴿takes away the sight﴾ means: because of the intensity of the light.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 24, verse 44:

And His saying: ﴿God alternates the night and the day﴾, meaning: He turns the night and the day around; the alternation (taqlib) of the night and the day is their succession, and this is the meaning of His exalted saying: ﴿He wraps the night over the day and wraps the day over the night﴾. It has been authentically related from the Prophet (ﷺ), by the transmission of Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, from Abu Hurayrah, that he said: "God, may He be exalted, says: The son of Adam harms Me by cursing time (al-dahr), though I am time (al-dahr). In My hand are the night and the day, and I turn them over."

He (may Allah be pleased with him) said: Al-Makki ibn Abd al-Razzaq informed us of this, saying: My grandfather Abu al-Haytham al-Farbri informed us, al-Bukhari informed us, al-Humaydi informed us, from Sufyan ibn Uyaynah, from al-Zuhri, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, the report.

It is also said: "God alternates the night and the day" means: He manages the affairs of the night and the day.

And His saying: ﴿Indeed in that is a lesson for those of insight﴾, meaning: a sign and an admonition for those of insight in the hearts. The grammarians claim that God mentioned "min" (from) three times in the first verse, and each of them has a meaning: His saying ﴿from the sky﴾ denotes the starting point (ibtida' al-ghayah), His saying ﴿from mountains﴾ denotes partition (tab'id), and His saying ﴿from hail﴾ denotes specification by kind (tajnis). Some of them have said regarding the second verse that the meaning of the alternation is that He takes away the night and brings the day, and takes away the day and brings the night.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 24, verse 45:

The words of the Exalted: ﴿And Allah created every creature from water.﴾ If someone says: How does His saying ﴿created every creature from water﴾ hold true, when He has created many living beings from other than water, such as the jinn and the angels? The answer to this: Allah the Exalted created all living beings from water. And the people of tafsir (exegesis) hold that Allah the Exalted created water, then turned it into fire, and from it He created the jinn; then He turned it into wind, and from it He created the angels; then He turned it into clay, and from it He created the children of Adam.

His saying: ﴿So among them is one that goes upon its belly﴾ means: like the snakes, the fish, and what resembles them. If it is said: How is walking upon the belly conceivable? The answer: what is meant by it is movement, and movement is general, both on limbs and on the belly. Some of them said: walking is used correctly for walking upon the belly; it is said: "mashā amru kadhā" (the matter proceeded thus).

His saying: ﴿And among them is one that walks on two legs﴾ means: like the children of Adam and the birds. If it is asked: Is a bird called a dābba (creature)? We say: Yes, because everything that crawls on the earth is a dābba.

His saying: ﴿And among them is one that walks on four﴾ means: the beasts. If it is said: We see things that walk on more than four, we say: al-Suddi mentioned that in the reading of Ubayy ibn Ka'b it is: "and among them is one that walks on more than four," so this serves as an explanation of the well-known reading, and it becomes as if Allah the Exalted said: ﴿among them is one that walks on four﴾ and on more than four. As for the well-known reading, He only mentioned four because, although the limbs may increase, the animal's reliance is on its four directions, so it is as if it walks on four. It is also said: even if it walks on more than four, it appears in form as though it walks on four. If it is said: He said ﴿among them [min] is one that walks﴾, and the word "min" is for rational beings, not for what lacks reason, the answer to this: He mentioned it with the word "min" because when speech gathers those who have reason and those who lack reason, the rational are given precedence over the non-rational.

His saying: ﴿Allah creates what He wills﴾ means: Allah creates what He wills beyond what has been mentioned.

His saying: ﴿And Allah is over all things Competent﴾: its meaning is clear.

The Exalted's saying: ﴿Indeed, We have sent down clear signs﴾. We have already explained it.

And His saying: ﴿And Allah guides whom He wills to a straight path﴾, meaning: the religion of truth, which is the straight path.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 24, verse 47:

His statement, the Exalted: ﴿They say, "We believe in Allah and the Messenger, and we obey."﴾ Al-Naqqash (al-Naqqash) mentioned that this verse was revealed concerning a hypocrite man named Bishr and a Jewish man, who had a dispute between them. The Jew said: "Let us go to judgment before Muhammad," and the hypocrite said: "Let us go to judgment before Ka'b ibn al-Ashraf." So Allah, the Exalted, revealed this verse concerning this hypocrite and those like him. Abu Bakr al-Farisi also cited in "Ahkam al-Qur'an" (Rulings of the Qur'an) that when the Prophet emigrated to Madinah, the Ansar gave him and the Muhajirun every land that water did not reach. The Messenger of Allah gave some of that to Uthman and Ali. Ali sold his share to Uthman, and Uthman found the land to be all stones that could not be cultivated. He asked Ali for the price he had paid him. Ali said: "And what do I know of stones? Had I found a treasure, would I have had any share of it?" So they wanted to go to judgment before the Prophet, but al-Hakam ibn Abi al-As said to Uthman: "Do not take him to judgment before Muhammad, for he will rule in favor of his cousin." So Allah, the Exalted, revealed this verse concerning al-Hakam ibn Abi al-As.

His statement: ﴿Then a party of them turn away after that.﴾ That is: after they had said, "We believe in Allah and the Messenger."

His statement: ﴿But those are not believers.﴾ That is: not those who affirm (al-musaddiqin).

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 24, verse 48:

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And when they are called to Allah and His Messenger, that he may judge between them﴾. Al-hukm (judgment) is the settling of a dispute in accordance with what the Shari'ah (sacred law) requires.

His saying: ﴿Behold, a party of them turn away﴾, i.e., away from the truth. It is also said: away from responding (to the call). The verse indicates that when a judge calls a person so that he may judge between him and his opponent, it becomes obligatory upon him to respond.
Allah's words: ﴿And if the right is theirs, they come to Him willingly, submissive﴾. That is, hastening, compliant, humbly obedient.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 24, verse 50:

And His saying: ﴿Is there a disease in their hearts?﴾ is a question in the sense of rebuke and censure, and its meaning is: an ailment that prevents them from accepting the truth.

And His saying: ﴿Or do they have doubt?﴾ means: they have doubted.

And His saying: ﴿Or do they fear that Allah and His Messenger will wrong them?﴾ The hayf (deviation, injustice) is inclining away from what is right without justification, and it is permissible to express it as oppression (zulm).

And His saying: ﴿Rather, it is they who are the wrongdoers.﴾ We have already explained this.

The Quranic verse: "The only saying of the believers, when they are called to Allah and His Messenger that he may judge between them, is that they say, 'We hear and we obey.'" (Actually translate as given.)

Let me give the translation directly:

The Almighty's words: ﴿The saying of the believers, when they are called to Allah and His Messenger that He may judge between them, is only that they say: "We hear and we obey." And those are the successful.﴾

This is not in the form of a report, but rather a teaching of etiquette from the Sharia, meaning that the believers should be like this.

His words: ﴿that they say, "We hear and we obey"﴾ meaning: We hear the call, and we obey by responding.

His words: ﴿And those are the ones who are successful﴾ meaning: the ones who attain success.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 24, verse 52:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger﴾, meaning: whoever obeys Allah in what He has commanded, and obeys His Messenger in what he has prescribed (sanna).

And His saying: ﴿and fears Allah﴾, meaning: concerning what has passed.

And His saying: ﴿and is mindful of Him﴾, meaning: he guards himself against Him concerning what is yet to come.

And His saying: ﴿then it is those who are the triumphant﴾, meaning: those who are saved.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 24, verse 53:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And they swore by Allah with their most solemn oaths﴾. The "most solemn oath" (jahd al-yamin) is that one swears by Allah. The people of knowledge said: there is no oath more emphatic than swearing by Allah.

And His saying: ﴿If you order them, they will surely go forth.﴾ That is: if you order them to go forth to jihad, they will surely go forth.

And His saying: ﴿Say: Do not swear.﴾ That is: do not take oaths.

And His saying: ﴿Obedience that is known (ta'ah ma'ruf).﴾ Concerning this there are several views. The first: let there be from you known obedience. The second: known obedience is better than an oath made with words that is not matched by belief. The third: this is known obedience from you, that you swear falsely and say what you do not do; and the meaning is: this is a known matter from you.

And His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah is Aware of what you do.﴾ Its meaning is apparent.

The Exalted's saying: ﴿Say: Obey Allah and obey the Messenger. But if you turn away﴾ — meaning: "if you turn away" (fa-in tatawallaw). It is also said: "if they turn away" (fa-in yatawallaw), shifting the address from direct address (al-muwajahah) to the third person (al-mughaybah).

And His saying: ﴿Upon him is only that with which he has been charged﴾ — meaning: upon the Messenger is what he has been charged with of conveying (al-tabligh).

﴿And upon you is that with which you have been charged﴾ — of responding (al-ijabah). That is: if you respond, then you will have the reward, and if you refuse, then upon you is the punishment.

And His saying: ﴿And if you obey him﴾ — meaning the Messenger — ﴿you will be guided﴾.

And His saying: ﴿And there is not upon the Messenger except the clear conveyance﴾ — meaning the clear (al-bayyin) conveyance of the message.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 24, verse 55:

His words, may He be exalted: ﴿Allah has promised those among you who believe and do righteous deeds﴾. Abu al-'Aliyah al-Riyahi said: Allah sent Muhammad, and he and his companions remained in Makkah for ten years, and they were commanded [to bear patience] ﴿Allah has promised those among you who believe and do righteous deeds that He will surely grant them succession upon the earth, just as He granted succession to those before them﴾ with patience over the harm of the disbelievers. They would wake up fearful and go to sleep fearful. Then he emigrated to Madinah, and they were commanded to fight while still in their fear, so no one among them would part from his weapon. A man among the Muslims said: "Will we not feel safe one day?" Then Allah, exalted is He, revealed this verse. Some of the exegetes mentioned that the companions of the Messenger of Allah wished to prevail over Makkah, so Allah, exalted is He, revealed this verse: ﴿Allah has promised those among you who believe and do righteous deeds that He will surely grant them succession upon the earth, just as He granted succession to those before them﴾. Qatadah said: "Just as He granted succession to Dawud, Sulayman and others among the prophets who held kingship."

The scholars have used this verse as evidence for the validity of the caliphate of the Rightly Guided Caliphs, who are: Abu Bakr, 'Umar, 'Uthman and 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with them all. Among the well-known reports transmitted through Hammad ibn Salamah, from Sa'id ibn Jumhan, from Safinah, that the Prophet said: "The caliphate after me will be thirty years."

He, may Allah be pleased with him, said: Abu al-Husayn ibn al-Naqur informed us of this hadith in Baghdad; Abu al-Qasim ibn Hababah informed us; Ibn Bint Mani' 'Abd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz al-Baghawi informed us, from Hudbah [ibn] Khalid, from Hammad ibn Salamah ... the report. It was recorded by Muslim in his Sahih.

His words: ﴿And He will surely establish for them their religion which He has approved for them﴾, meaning: He will surely make their religion prevail over all other religions. The scholars said: this refers to Persia, Rome and those like them. In some strange reports it is related that the Prophet said: "There is no house of adobe or of hair in the earth except that Allah will cause the religion to enter it, ﴿And He will surely establish for them their religion which He has approved for them, and will surely replace their fear with security﴾, Islam, willingly or unwillingly."

His words: ﴿approved for them﴾ meaning: chose for them.

It is established from the Prophet that he said to 'Adi ibn Hatim: "Allah will surely make this religion prevail, until a woman travelling alone will leave al-Hirah heading to the House of Allah, fearing none but Allah and the wolf concerning her sheep." 'Adi ibn Hatim said: "I said to myself: then where are the highwaymen?" 'Adi said: "And indeed I saw what the Messenger of Allah had said."

His words: ﴿and will surely replace their fear with security﴾. This is what we have mentioned. It has been related that the companions of the Messenger of Allah, while they were in Makkah, would not pray except in hiding, and each one of them would guard his companion until he prayed, and his companion would guard him until he prayed. Then, when they emigrated, they were secure, and they worshipped Allah openly, and security kept increasing until our time... the hadith.

His words: ﴿They worship Me, not associating anything with Me﴾, meaning: they worship Me in security and without associating [partners with Me].

His words: ﴿And whoever disbelieves after that, those are the defiantly disobedient﴾. Most of the exegetes hold that disbelief here is not disbelief in Allah; rather, what is intended is ingratitude for the blessing by abandoning obedience. Therefore He said: ﴿those are the defiantly disobedient﴾. Some of them said: it is disbelief in Allah, but the more correct view is the first.
Almighty Allah's saying: ﴿And establish prayer, and give zakat, and obey the Messenger, that you may receive mercy.﴾ That is: do these things in hope of receiving mercy.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 24, verse 57:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Do not think that those who disbelieve will escape [Us] in the earth﴾. Its meaning: do not suppose that those who disbelieve will get away from Us in the manner of one who escapes from someone we are unable to overpower. The real meaning is: We are not unable to overpower any of them. (And they have nothing with which they could be self-sufficient, so that they would be in the position of those who render others unable to reach them.)

And His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Their refuge is the Fire, and wretched is the destination﴾. That is: and wretched is the place of return.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 24, verse 58:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿O you who have believed, let those whom your right hands possess ask your permission﴾ — there are several opinions regarding it. Mujahid said: "Those whom your right hands possess are the slaves." It is also reported from some of them that they are the female slaves (imaa', sing. amah), and this is narrated from Ibn Umar. The more correct view is that it refers to both male and female slaves.

His saying: ﴿And those among you who have not reached puberty (al-hulm)﴾ — these are not the ones who have not yet come to know the nakedness of women, for those who have not come to know the nakedness of women have no modesty (hishmah) with respect to anyone among them, because we have explained that they are those who do not yet discern. Rather, these are the ones who have discerned and have come to know matters concerning women, but have not reached puberty.

His saying: ﴿three times﴾ — meaning: they should ask permission three times.

And His saying: ﴿before the prayer of dawn, and when you put off your clothes at midday, and after the prayer of the night﴾ — He singled out these three times for the command to ask permission, because they are times when people become uncovered and expose what they do not wish anyone to see. Before dawn, they awaken from sleep and so become uncovered; at midday they take off their clothes to rest; and after the (final) night prayer they become uncovered for sleep. So God, Exalted is He, commanded asking permission at these three times for this meaning. The intent of the verse is the asking of permission by servants and children; as for others, they ask permission in all circumstances. ﴿Three times for you: before the prayer of dawn, and when you put off your clothes at midday, and after the prayer of the night — three times of nakedness (awrat) for you. There is no blame on you or on them beyond these (times)﴾.

It is related from Ibn Abbas that he said: "The people did not have curtains or [partitions], and the servants and slave girls would enter upon them and see from them what they did not wish to be seen. So God, Exalted is He, commanded asking permission. Then God expanded their provision, and the people took curtains and [screens], and they saw that this had made asking permission unnecessary." Al-Sha'bi and Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: "This verse is not abrogated, but people have become negligent." Ata related from Ibn Abbas that he said: "There are three verses of the Qur'an which people do not act upon." He mentioned this verse, and he mentioned His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, the most noble of you in the sight of God is the most righteous of you﴾. "So people keep saying: 'I am the son of so-and-so, and more noble than so-and-so, and better than so-and-so.'" Ata said: "And I have forgotten the third."

His saying: ﴿three nakedness-times for you﴾ — it is read with the "th" (thalath) in the nominative and in the accusative. Thus His saying ﴿three﴾ in the nominative means: "they are three times of nakedness for you." And His saying ﴿three times of nakedness for you﴾ in the accusative is a substitution (badal) for His saying "three times," so it is accusative by way of substitution.

His saying: ﴿there is no blame on you or on them﴾ — meaning: there is no sin in neglecting to ask permission at other than these three times.

His saying: ﴿after them﴾ — an indication of this meaning.

His saying: ﴿They go round about you, some of you attending to others﴾ — a beginning (of a new statement), meaning: these servants and slave girls go round about you, moving among you to serve you. From this is his saying concerning the cat: "Indeed, it is one of those who go round about you, male and female."

His saying: ﴿some of you attending to others﴾ — meaning: some of you go round attending to others.

His saying: ﴿Thus God makes the signs clear to you﴾ — meaning: the proofs; and it has been said: the rulings.

His saying: ﴿And God is All-Knowing, All-Wise﴾ — meaning: All-Knowing of the affairs of His creation, All-Wise in what He has ordained for them.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 24, verse 59:

And His, may He be exalted, saying: ﴿And when the children among you reach puberty, let them ask permission﴾. His saying: ﴿reach puberty﴾ means: the ihtilam (wet dream, i.e., the nocturnal emission that marks the onset of puberty). His saying: ﴿let them ask permission﴾ (as those who were adults asked permission, and it is said) ﴿as those who were before them asked permission﴾, meaning: as those who were before them asked permission (along with Ibrahim, Musa and Isa).

And His saying: ﴿Thus does Allah make clear to you His verses﴾ means: His rulings.

And His saying: ﴿And Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise﴾ has already been explained.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 24, verse 60:

His statement, exalted is He: ﴿And women past child-bearing﴾. Al-qawa'id is the plural of qa'id. It is said: "a woman qa'id" when she has ceased from men (marriage), when she has ceased from menstruation due to old age. As for qa'ida, it means the one who sits (remains seated).

And His statement: ﴿who do not hope for marriage﴾ means: they do not desire marriage. It was also said: they do not desire men because of their old age. It was also said: they have ceased from activity due to old age. It is said "a woman qa'id" when she has grown old only because she sits (stays at home) often; this was said by Ibn Qutayba.

On the authority of Rabi'a al-Ra'y, he said: They are the old women whom men find repulsive. As for the one who still retains some beauty, which is the seat of desire, she does not enter into this verse.

And His statement: ﴿there is no blame upon them﴾, meaning: no sin.

And His statement: ﴿that they lay aside their outer garments﴾. In the recitation of Ibn Mas'ud: "that they lay aside some of their garments." He recited: ﴿who do not hope for marriage, there is no blame upon them that they lay aside their garments, not displaying adornment﴾. Ibn Mas'ud said: "Their garments here are the cloak (ridaʾ) and the outer wrap (jilbab)." On the authority of Ibn 'Abbas, he said: the jilbab. As for the khimar, it is not permissible for her to put it aside; but the garment that is worn over the khimar, it is permissible for her to put aside.

In some reports: for the husband is what is beneath the shift (dir')... and for a close relative (dhu al-mahram) is what is above the shift, and for a non-mahram is what is above the shift, the cloak, the outer wrap, the jilbab and the khimar.

And His statement: ﴿without displaying adornment﴾, meaning: by laying aside the cloak and the jilbab they should not intend to show their adornment and charms. The root of tabarruj is manifestation. Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿and do not display yourselves as in the former days of ignorance﴾, meaning: do not uncover yourselves as in the former days of ignorance. In the exegesis: when a woman walks before men, she has displayed herself as in the former days of ignorance.

It is established from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "I have left after me no trial more harmful to men than women." Narrated by Usama.

It was said to some of the wise: "What is the most affectionate of beasts?" He said: "The woman." And one of them said to another: "No evil has ever entered the door of my house." He said: "From where does your wife enter?" [And] one of them saw a crucified woman and said: "If every tree bore fruit like this, people would be saved from a great evil."

And His statement: ﴿and that they refrain (yasta'fifna) is better for them﴾, meaning: that they do not lay aside the cloak and the jilbab is better for them. On the authority of 'Asim al-Ahwal, he said: "We used to enter upon Hafsa, and she was wrapped in her jilbab, covered with her cloak and veiled, so we said to her: 'O Mother of the Believers, are you not among the al-qawa'id?' Then she recited His statement, exalted is He: ﴿and that they refrain is better for them﴾."

And His statement: ﴿and Allah is All-Hearing, All-Knowing﴾, whose meaning is apparent.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 24, verse 61:

His words, may He be exalted: {There is no blame upon the blind, nor upon the lame, nor upon the sick, [for going out to war]} (the verse). Scholars differed concerning this verse. Al-Hasan al-Basri said: the verse was revealed concerning the dispensation granted to these people to remain behind from the jihad. What is mentioned after it, concerning eating, is an adjoining of one dispensation to another dispensation.

It is related from Ibn 'Abbas that he said: the verse was revealed concerning the dispensation to eat, from its beginning to its end. The reason for this is that people used to feel scrupulous about eating with the blind, the lame and the sick. They would say: the blind man does not eat his fill, the lame man (eats) from sitting, and the sick man is too weak to reach for food. These (disabled) people also felt scrupulous about eating with the healthy. The blind man would say: I will not eat with one who can see, for I may eat more than he does. The lame man would say: I may take the place of two people. The sick man would say: people find me repulsive. So God, may He be exalted, revealed this verse and lifted the blame.

The third opinion: people used to go out to raids and leave these people in their houses, and they (the ones left behind) felt scrupulous about eating. So God, may He be exalted, revealed this verse and lifted the blame. This is the view of 'A'isha.

The fourth opinion: these people would enter upon a man seeking food and find nothing, so that man would go to another house and take them with himself, so that they might partake of that man's food. This is the view of Mujahid.

It is related from 'Abd al-Karim al-Jazari that he said: what is meant by the verse is the blind man who has a guide; his guide carries him so that he may eat with him. Likewise the lame and the sick may carry a person with themselves.

His words: {Nor upon yourselves that you eat from your houses}, meaning: there is no blame upon yourselves that you eat from your houses. Concerning its meaning there are two views. The first: it means the houses of your children. It is related from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "You and your wealth belong to your father."

{Your houses, or the houses of your fathers, or the houses of your mothers, or the houses of your brothers, or the houses of your sisters, or the houses of your paternal uncles, or the houses of your paternal aunts, or the houses of your maternal uncles, or the houses of}

The second view: what is meant is the houses of spouses. It is said: each person's house is his own, and the children are more apparent (as the meaning).

His words: {or the houses of your fathers} to the end of the verse are clear in meaning.

His words: {or what you possess the keys of} Ibn 'Abbas said: this refers to a man's agent and steward over his estate and his flock; he eats from the dates and drinks from the milk, but does not carry away or hoard. The second view: what is meant by the verse is the houses of slaves. The keys (mafatih) are the treasuries. God, may He be exalted, said: {and with Him are the keys of the unseen} (42 ... 6:59), meaning: the treasuries of the unseen.

His words: {or your friend}. The friend (al-siddiq) is the one who is sincere to you in affection. It is said: the friend is the one whose outward is like your outward and whose inward is like your inward. The word "friend" here is singular in meaning but collective.

The poet said:

([They called] to desire, [then] they shot at our hearts ... with arrows of enemies, and they are (also) friends)

It is related from some of them that God, may He be exalted, placed the rank of a friend above the rank of the two parents. God, may He be exalted, said, relating the words of the people of Hell: {So we have no intercessors, nor any warm friend} (26:100–101). It is related from Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq that he said: the likeness of your friend is the likeness of yourself. It is related from al-Hasan and Qatada that they said: they used to prefer to enter the houses of their brothers and take from them without asking permission, and this would happen with good will from their hearts and affection in their hearts. It is related from Ibn 'Umar that he said: none of us had a better claim to his companion's dirham and dinar than the other.

It is related from some of them that he mentioned a friend of his and said: would he take from your purse ... and your dirhams, that which you love, and not dislike it? He said: No. He said: then he is not a friend to you.

His words: {There is no blame upon you that you eat together or separately}. It is related that when God, may He be exalted, revealed His words: {And do not consume your wealth among yourselves in falsehood, except that it be trade by mutual consent} (4:29), the people became extremely cautious, and they said: we will not eat with anyone, lest we eat falsely. So God, may He be exalted, revealed this verse. It is also related that the verse was revealed concerning Malik ibn Zayd with al-Harith ibn 'Amr: al-Harith was left by Malik ibn Zayd in his house, and he went out on a raid, and he permitted him to eat, but he ate nothing. It is well known in exegesis that the verse was revealed concerning the Banu Bakr of Kinana: none of them would eat alone until he found a guest to eat with him. If he did not find one and hunger overcame him, he would set up a piece of wood, drape a garment over it, and eat in front of it, so that people would think he was a person eating with him. It is related that one of them alighted with his milch-camels in a valley and became hungry, so he milked one of the camels and called out in the valley: whoever is here, let him come and eat. There was a man in the valley who hid himself and did not respond, and hunger overcame him, so he sat and ate alone. The man came out and said to him: O suckling one, do you eat alone? So the man took his sword, attacked him and killed him, out of fear that this deed of his would spread among the people. Then God, may He be exalted, revealed this verse and permitted the people to eat either individually or in company.

If it is asked: what is your view on this verse, and if one of those previously mentioned enters a house, may he eat without its owner's permission? The answer: Abu Bakr al-Farisi said: if permission was given by him in general terms, even if it was not specified, then he may eat; but with others than these it is not permitted unless it is specified. Some of them said: if the food is freely available and not guarded, it is permissible for him to eat; but if it is kept in a secured store, it is not permissible for him to eat. As for carrying provisions and dispensing with another's property, it is forbidden unless permission is given specifically. It has also been said: if it is a small amount, there is no harm in it for slaves and servants.

His words: {So when you enter houses, greet one another} meaning: let some of you greet others. This is like His words: {and do not kill yourselves} (4:29), meaning: let some of you not kill others. It is said that the meaning of the verse is: when one enters his house, he should greet his family. This is a sunnah that has been abandoned. Qatada said: your family has more right that you greet them. Al-Awza'i, when he entered his house and forgot the greeting, would go out, then return and greet. As for when one enters an empty house, he says: "Peace be upon us from our Lord." When he enters a mosque in which there is no one, he says: "Peace be upon us and upon the righteous servants of God." We have already explained that the sunnah is to spread the greeting of peace to those you know and to those you do not know. Ibn 'Umar used to greet women just as he greeted men. They (the scholars) said: if she is an old woman, there is no harm in it; but if she is young, one should not greet her.

His words: {a greeting from God, blessed and good}, meaning: beautiful and pleasant, as said by Ibn 'Abbas. It is also said: the mention of blessing and goodness here is because of the reward it contains. Whoever offers a greeting of peace to a person has given a gift that is light to carry, good in fragrance, and blessed in its consequence.

His words: {Thus God makes the signs clear to you, that you may understand} the meaning is apparent.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 24, verse 62:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿The believers are only those who have believed in Allah and His Messenger, and when they are with him on a matter of common concern, they do not leave until they have asked his permission﴾. This is teaching one of the courtesies (adab) of Islam. "A matter of common concern" (amr jami') refers to anything that gathers the Muslims together. It has been said that it is jihad; it is said that it is the Friday prayer and the two festivals; and it is said that it is every act of obedience around which the Muslims gather together with the imam.

In the reports (akhbar): "A man among the Muslims, when he was with the Prophet in some matter and wished to seek permission for a need of his, would stand and gesture toward the Prophet as if asking permission, and the Prophet would gesture to him: 'I have given you permission.'" It has been said: permission is only needed when there is no reason preventing one from remaining. But if a reason arises that prevents one from remaining, such as a woman in the mosque who begins menstruating, or a man who becomes junub (in a state of major ritual impurity), or who falls ill, and the like, then he does not need to seek permission.

His saying: ﴿Indeed, those who ask your permission are those who believe in Allah and His Messenger﴾. It is narrated that Umar asked the Messenger of Allah for permission during the Battle of Tabuk to return to his family, and he said: "Go back, for you are not a hypocrite nor a doubter," thereby contrasting him with the hypocrites. It has also been said that this verse abrogates (naskh) His saying, Exalted is He, in Surah at-Tawbah: ﴿Allah pardon you! Why did you give them permission?﴾

His saying: ﴿So when they ask your permission for some of their affairs﴾, meaning: their matters.

His saying: ﴿So permit whom you will of them﴾ means: if you wish, grant permission, and if you wish, do not grant it.

﴿And ask forgiveness for them from Allah. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾, meaning: supplicate for them when they ask you to supplicate for them.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 24, verse 63:

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿Do not make the summoning of the Messenger among yourselves like the summoning of some of you by others﴾ mean: do not say, "O Muhammad, O Abu'l-Qasim, O son of Abdullah," but say, "O Messenger of Allah, O Prophet," and address him with reverence and honour.

His words: ﴿Allah already knows those who slip away﴾. At-tasallul (slipping away) is leaving secretly. The hypocrites used to do this. Attending the mosque, remaining in it, and listening to the Prophet's sermon were burdensome to them, so some of them would signal to one another and leave the mosque.

His words: ﴿liwadhan﴾ mean: some of them take cover behind others. It was also said: [it means] "rahlan" (moving away on foot).

His words: ﴿So let those who oppose his command beware﴾ mean: his command.

His words: ﴿lest a trial befall them﴾ mean: lest a trial, that is, an affliction, befall them.

His words: ﴿or a painful punishment strike them﴾. It is said: the painful punishment is in this world, and it is said: it is in the Hereafter.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 24, verse 64:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Surely to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth. He knows well your state﴾. That is: He knows. The word "qad" is a filler (ṣila).

And His saying: ﴿And the day they are returned to Him﴾ means: in the Hereafter.

And His saying: ﴿Then He will inform them of what they did﴾, that is: Allah will inform them of what they did.

And His saying: ﴿And Allah is All-Knowing of everything﴾, that is: Knowing (ʿālim).

Completed, by the praise of Allah the Exalted, is the third volume of the Tafsir of Abu al-Muzaffar al-Sam'ani, and it is followed by the fourth volume, God willing, whose beginning is the tafsir of Surat al-Furqan.
